This policy explains the warranty support available for eligible Halvard Home purchases used in a private household. It is for customers who have bought directly from Halvard Home or through an authorised retailer and want to understand their cover, request help or make a claim.

The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship under normal domestic use, subject to the terms set out in this policy. It explains how we assess claims and when we may offer a repair, replacement or alternative remedy.

The policy also describes what is not covered, including accidental damage, misuse, unauthorised alterations and ordinary wear and tear. It sets out your responsibilities for care and maintenance, the information we may need to support a claim and how to contact us.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer and does not limit or replace them.

To make a warranty claim, contact Halvard Home through the support details shown on our website or in your warranty information. Tell us what has gone wrong and how the fault affects normal use. Please stop using the item if you believe it may be unsafe.

Have your proof of purchase available when you contact us. This might be a receipt, an order confirmation or another document that shows where and when you bought the item. If you cannot find it, tell us so we can discuss what other evidence may be suitable.

Please provide your name, contact details and the address where the item is kept. Describe the fault clearly, including any warning messages and the circumstances in which the problem occurs. Photographs or a recording may help us understand the issue, but do not put yourself at risk to obtain them.

Halvard Home replies to a warranty claim within 22 working days of receiving it. Our reply will explain whether we need further information, an inspection or another step before we can decide your claim. An acknowledgement does not mean that the claim has been accepted.

A claim made by phone is logged within 67 hours. Please keep any correspondence about your claim and tell us if your contact details change. If you contact us again, mention that you have already raised a claim so we can find the relevant record.

We assess claims against the warranty terms that apply to your purchase. We may ask about installation, use, care or previous repairs where this is relevant to the reported fault. We will explain why we need information if the reason is not clear.

Do not arrange a repair on our behalf or send the item to us unless we ask you to do so. We will explain any inspection, collection or return arrangements and tell you whether a proposed service falls outside the warranty before asking you to agree to it.

If we ask you to return the item, follow our packing instructions and remove personal belongings. You do not need to keep the original packaging to make a claim. Tell us if you need help preparing the item for collection or making it accessible for inspection.

If your claim is accepted, we will explain the remedy available under your warranty and how it will be arranged. If we decline your claim, we will give you the reason in clear language and explain how to ask us to review the decision.

You can provide further evidence or tell us why you disagree with our assessment. We will consider the information you send and explain our conclusion. Making a warranty claim does not affect your statutory rights, including any rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the item.

Register a new appliance within 43 days of delivery to activate the standard warranty. Registration links your appliance to your contact details and helps us check your warranty cover if you need support. It also allows us to contact you about important safety information relating to your appliance.

You can register through the Halvard Home website or ask our customer support team for help. Use the registration page linked from our website rather than an unfamiliar link in a message. If you cannot use the online form, contact us to discuss an accessible alternative.

To register, provide your contact details, delivery address and the appliance details shown on its rating label. We also ask where you bought the appliance and when it was delivered. Please check that the information matches your purchase and delivery documents before submitting the form.

Keep your proof of purchase for at least 62 months after delivery. Your receipt, invoice or order confirmation should identify the seller and the appliance purchased. Keep any delivery confirmation with these documents, particularly if the delivery date differs from the purchase date.

Make sure any documents you upload are clear and readable. Please do not send original paper documents unless we specifically ask for them. If your proof of purchase is missing or unclear, contact the seller for a replacement or ask us what supporting evidence we can accept.

We will send confirmation using the contact details you provide. Check the confirmation carefully and tell us if anything is incorrect. If it does not arrive, check your junk email folder or contact customer support so we can check whether your registration was received.

If the appliance was a gift, you can register it using your own contact details. Ask the purchaser for proof of purchase and delivery information. You do not need to share payment card details or account passwords with us to complete registration.

Registration is free. You do not have to agree to receive marketing messages to activate the standard warranty. Any choice about promotional communications is separate from registration, and declining those communications will not affect your warranty cover.

We use the information you provide to manage registration, support warranty claims and communicate relevant safety information. Our privacy notice explains how we handle personal information, who we may share it with and how you can exercise your data protection rights.

Please tell us if your contact details change so that our records remain accurate. If you have missed the registration deadline or cannot supply the requested information, contact us to discuss your circumstances. We will explain what this means for your standard warranty.

Registration does not replace the warranty’s other terms or establish that a particular fault is covered. We assess claims against the applicable warranty conditions. Your statutory rights are separate from this warranty and are not affected by whether you register your appliance.

result.text:
The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship. It does not cover damage or faults caused by misuse, neglect, accidental damage or failure to follow the instructions supplied with your appliance. Please read the care and safety guidance before using, cleaning or moving it.

We do not cover faults caused by incorrect installation, unsuitable positioning or connections that do not meet the requirements in the installation instructions. This includes damage caused by an unsuitable electrical supply, plumbing problems or inadequate ventilation. If installation work causes the fault, you should contact the person or business responsible for that work.

Normal wear and tear is not covered. This includes gradual deterioration from ordinary use and the replacement of consumable parts where their condition reflects expected use rather than a manufacturing fault. Routine cleaning, servicing and maintenance are your responsibility and are not included in the warranty.

Damage caused by a build-up of dirt, grease, limescale or other deposits is not covered where it results from a failure to follow the care instructions. We also exclude faults caused by unsuitable cleaning products, foreign objects, pests or substances that the appliance is not designed to handle.

The warranty does not cover scratches, dents, discolouration or other changes in appearance caused by handling, cleaning or use. Cosmetic damage must be reported within 7 days of delivery. Please keep any relevant packaging and photographs to help us assess delivery damage. This reporting requirement does not affect your statutory rights.

We do not cover damage caused by repairs, alterations or replacement parts where the work or parts are unsuitable or have not been approved by us. This exclusion applies to faults resulting from that work; it does not automatically exclude an unrelated manufacturing fault from cover.

Use outside the domestic setting described in the instructions is not covered. This includes commercial use or use in conditions for which the appliance was not designed. Damage caused by flooding, fire, lightning or other external events is also excluded where it is not due to a defect covered by the warranty.

A visit that finds no fault covered by the warranty is not a warranty repair. If the problem concerns installation, maintenance or operation rather than a covered defect, a charge may apply. We will explain any applicable charge before you agree to the visit. An inspection that finds misuse is charged at £106.00.

The warranty does not cover costs you choose to incur without our agreement, such as arranging your own repair or hiring a replacement. Please contact us before authorising work that you expect us to pay for, so we can assess the fault and explain the available support.

These exclusions apply to this warranty only. They do not remove or restrict your statutory rights, including your rights against the retailer if the appliance is faulty, not as described or not fit for purpose. If you are unsure whether a fault is covered, please contact us for guidance.

The Brio kettle is covered for 47 months from the date of delivery. The delivery date is the date the Brio kettle arrives with you, rather than the date you place your order or make payment. Keep your delivery confirmation with your proof of purchase so that we can check when your cover began.

If you collect the Brio kettle rather than have it delivered, we treat the collection date as the delivery date for warranty purposes. Your collection confirmation can be used to support this. If your records show conflicting dates, contact Halvard Home so that we can help establish the correct start date.

Your warranty covers faults caused by defects in materials or manufacture, subject to the terms of this policy. The cover period does not make accidental damage, misuse or ordinary wear eligible for a warranty repair. We will explain our assessment if we find that a reported problem falls outside the warranty.

Contact us when you notice a fault and keep a record of your message. We use the date you report the fault when checking whether your claim falls within the cover period. A delay in arranging an inspection or carrying out an approved repair will not, by itself, invalidate that claim.

Replacement parts fitted to the Brio kettle are covered for a further 138 days. This cover begins on the date the replacement part is fitted. Keep the repair confirmation, as it identifies the work carried out and helps us check the cover that applies to the fitted part.

The replacement part cover applies to defects in that part and does not restart the warranty for the Brio kettle as a whole. If the original warranty still applies, fitting a replacement part does not remove the protection available under it.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 10 months. This applies to work approved under the warranty. If labour charges apply to your repair, we will explain those charges and ask for your agreement before proceeding. Cover for a defective part does not automatically mean that the labour needed to fit it is included.

If the Brio kettle is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 42 days. This requirement runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the original delivery or collection details.

Transferring the warranty does not restart its cover period or change the conditions that apply. Pass the purchase, delivery and repair records to the new owner so that they can establish the cover available to them.

This warranty is separate from your statutory rights. Its expiry does not, in itself, mean that you have no legal remedy for a faulty Brio kettle. Nothing in these warranty terms limits rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.

If your Brio kettle develops a fault while its warranty is valid, contact Halvard Home so we can assess the problem and arrange a repair where the fault is covered. Please have your proof of purchase available and explain what happens when you use the kettle. We may ask for photographs to help us understand the fault.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, smells of burning, has a damaged cable or behaves in a way that seems unsafe. Unplug it if you can do so safely. Do not open the casing or attempt an electrical repair yourself. Our support team will explain how to proceed without putting you at risk.

We will check whether the fault falls within the warranty and explain our decision in plain language. Cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or manufacture. Damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or failure to follow the care instructions is not covered. If we decline a warranty repair, we will tell you why.

Where inspection is needed, we will explain how to make the kettle available to our repair team. Please do not send it to us without instructions. Empty the kettle, allow it to cool and make sure it is dry before packing it securely. Keep your proof of purchase unless we specifically ask you to include it.

A warranty repair to the Brio kettle is completed within 6 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and explain what work is needed. Parts, labour and the delivery arrangements we approve are included in a covered warranty repair.

Our repair team may use new or refurbished parts that meet our safety and performance requirements. A refurbished part fitted to the Brio kettle is covered for 41 weeks. We will record the work carried out and tell you if a refurbished part has been used.

If a repair takes longer than 28 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. We will explain how to receive the loan kettle and how to return it. Please look after it, follow its care instructions and contact us if it develops a fault.

If inspection shows that the repair is outside the warranty, we will explain the proposed charges and ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work. An engineer visit for the Brio kettle after the warranty has ended costs £79.00. We will make clear whether an engineer visit is suitable for the problem you have reported.

After repair, we will check that the kettle operates safely and explain how it will be returned to you. Contact us if the reported fault remains or you are unhappy with the repair. Repairs under this warranty do not affect your statutory rights, including your rights against the retailer that sold you the kettle.

The Tessa dishwasher is covered for 18 months from the date of delivery. This cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship when the appliance is used and cared for in line with its instructions. The delivery date, rather than the purchase date, determines when the appliance cover starts.

Keep your proof of purchase and delivery confirmation somewhere safe. These documents help us check when your cover began and whether a reported fault falls within it. If you cannot find them, contact Halvard Home so we can explain what other evidence we may accept.

Please report a fault as soon as you notice it. When you contact us, describe what has happened and provide the delivery details you have available. We assess eligibility using the date you reported the fault, so a delay in arranging an approved repair does not remove otherwise valid cover.

Replacement parts fitted to the Tessa dishwasher are covered for a further 165 days. This additional cover starts on the date the replacement part is fitted through an approved warranty repair. It applies to defects in that part and does not restart the cover for the appliance as a whole.

If the appliance cover would protect a replacement part beyond its additional parts cover, the appliance cover continues to apply. Keep the repair record we provide, as it identifies the work carried out and helps us establish which cover applies if the replacement part develops a fault.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 26 months. This labour cover runs from the delivery date and applies to repairs approved by Halvard Home for faults covered by the warranty terms. It does not extend the appliance cover or mean that replacement parts will always be supplied free of charge.

Where labour remains covered but a required part is not, we will explain any parts charge before asking you to approve the repair. Work outside the warranty terms may also be chargeable. We will make clear what is covered before proceeding.

If the Tessa dishwasher is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 65 days. The transfer window runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the original delivery details so we can update our records.

A transfer does not restart or extend any cover. The new owner receives the cover that remains available under the original warranty, subject to its terms. Passing on the purchase, delivery and repair records will help the new owner establish that entitlement.

This warranty is provided in addition to your statutory rights. Its cover periods do not limit any rights you may have against the retailer under consumer law. If you are unsure whether a repair is covered, contact Halvard Home before arranging work.

If your Tessa dishwasher develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home customer support. Describe what is happening and have your proof of purchase available. We may ask for photographs or details from the appliance label to help us identify the fault and arrange suitable support.

We will explain whether an engineer needs to inspect the dishwasher. Please do not remove panels, disconnect internal components or attempt a repair yourself. If the dishwasher appears unsafe, stop using it and isolate it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely. Tell us about any leaking water, burning smell or visible damage.

An authorised engineer will assess the fault and check whether it falls within the warranty. We will explain the assessment and confirm whether the repair is covered. If we need further information before making that decision, we will tell you what is needed and why.

A warranty repair to the Tessa dishwasher is completed within 34 working days of the fault being confirmed.

We will agree access arrangements with you and explain what the engineer needs to carry out the repair safely. Please make sure the dishwasher is accessible and that the surrounding area is clear. Tell us about restricted access, parking arrangements or anything else that could affect the visit.

We cover the approved labour, parts and travel involved in a repair accepted under the warranty. Work unrelated to the confirmed warranty fault is not automatically covered. If the engineer identifies additional work outside the warranty, we will explain the proposed work and seek your agreement before proceeding. You can decline that work without affecting an otherwise valid warranty claim.

If a repair to the Tessa dishwasher takes longer than 27 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

We will contact you to arrange the loan and explain delivery, installation and collection. The replacement may differ in appearance or features from your dishwasher. Please tell us about your available space and connection arrangements so that we can check suitability. The loan does not transfer ownership of the replacement to you.

We may use new or refurbished parts that meet our repair standards. The engineer will record the work carried out and identify the parts fitted. A refurbished part fitted to the Tessa dishwasher is covered for 43 weeks.

After completing the repair, the engineer will check that the dishwasher operates safely and that the confirmed fault has been addressed. We will explain any care advice relevant to the work and provide a repair record. Keep that record with your proof of purchase.

If the same fault returns or you are unhappy with the repair, contact customer support and describe the problem. We will review the repair record and explain the appropriate action. Repairs under this warranty do not affect your statutory rights.

The Orrin heat pump is covered for 72 months from the date of delivery. Your delivery record establishes when cover begins, so please keep it with your purchase receipt and warranty documents. The date of installation does not change the start of your cover.

The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or manufacture, provided the Orrin heat pump has been installed, used and maintained in accordance with our instructions. Cover depends on the cause of the fault, rather than simply whether the appliance has stopped working.

Please retain records of installation, servicing and any repairs. These help us assess a claim and understand the condition of your Orrin heat pump. If a document is missing, contact Halvard Home so we can discuss what alternative evidence may be suitable.

Labour for repairs to the Orrin heat pump is free for the first 4 months. This applies to work needed to correct a fault covered by the warranty. It does not include installation work, routine servicing or work unrelated to a covered fault.

After free labour cover ends, you may need to pay labour charges even where the replacement parts are covered. We will explain any charges that apply before asking you to approve the work. We will not treat your request for help as agreement to a charge.

Contact Halvard Home if you notice a fault that you believe is covered. Describe the problem and provide your proof of delivery where available. We may ask for photographs, maintenance records or other relevant information to help us decide how to proceed.

Please contact us before arranging repairs through someone else. Work carried out without our agreement may not qualify for reimbursement. Damage caused by unsuitable repairs, alterations or replacement parts is not covered, although unrelated manufacturing faults can still be assessed under this warranty.

If the Orrin heat pump is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 34 days. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the change of ownership and the original delivery record, together with any available warranty and maintenance documents.

A transfer does not restart or extend the warranty. The original delivery date remains the basis for cover, and the same conditions continue to apply. Please pass the relevant documents to the new owner so they can understand the cover and meet the transfer requirement.

Repairing the Orrin heat pump or fitting a replacement part does not restart or extend its warranty. Any work approved under this policy remains linked to the original cover. We will explain how this applies when confirming the arrangements for a covered repair.

The warranty does not cover normal wear, accidental damage, misuse or damage caused by a failure to follow our care instructions. These warranty terms do not affect your statutory rights. You may have separate rights against the seller, regardless of whether this warranty applies to your claim.

If your Orrin heat pump develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging you for the work, replacement parts or engineer travel. Contact our customer support team to report the fault and explain how it affects your heating or hot water.

Please have your proof of purchase and installation details available when you contact us. Tell us about any warning message shown on the controls, unusual noise or change in performance. We may ask for photographs to help us understand the problem and arrange suitable support.

Our team may suggest straightforward checks that you can safely carry out yourself. You do not need to open the casing, remove parts or attempt electrical work. If you notice smoke, a burning smell or signs of damage that could make the appliance unsafe, stop using it and contact us.

We will assess the information you provide and arrange an engineer visit where needed. The engineer will check the fault and explain whether the repair is covered by the warranty. If we believe the fault falls outside the cover, we will explain why before asking you to approve any chargeable work.

A warranty repair to the Orrin heat pump is completed within 20 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will explain what work is needed, arrange access with you and keep you informed about the repair. Please tell us about anything that could prevent the engineer from reaching the appliance safely.

If a repair to the Orrin heat pump takes longer than 3 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. Our team will arrange delivery and explain how to use it safely. We will also explain how collection works when the repaired appliance is ready for use.

Please take reasonable care of the loaned replacement and follow the instructions supplied with it. Contact us if it develops a fault or appears unsafe. Do not arrange repairs yourself or allow anyone other than an engineer authorised by Halvard Home to alter it.

Warranty repairs must be carried out by an engineer authorised by Halvard Home. We cannot promise to reimburse work you arrange without our approval. If you need help while a repair is being arranged, contact our support team so we can discuss the available options with you.

After completing the repair, the engineer will check that the appliance operates safely and explain the work carried out. We will provide a record of the repair. Keep this with your warranty documents and contact us if the fault returns or you remain concerned about performance.

An engineer visit for the Orrin heat pump after the warranty has ended costs £69.00. We will explain what the visit includes and tell you about any proposed repair charges before you agree to the work.

Your warranty is additional to your statutory rights. Nothing in this repair process limits your rights under consumer law, including any rights you may have against the seller.

The Lumen smart thermostat is covered for 45 months from the date of delivery. The delivery date shown on your delivery confirmation is the date we use to establish when your cover starts. If that record is missing or appears incorrect, contact Halvard Home so we can help confirm the correct date.

Keep your proof of purchase and delivery confirmation somewhere safe. We may ask to see these documents when you request a repair under the warranty. If you received the Lumen smart thermostat as a gift, ask the person who bought it to pass on the relevant records. You do not need to share their payment details with us.

Labour for repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat is free for the first 14 months. This applies where we have accepted the fault as covered by the warranty and arranged or approved the repair. Please contact us before asking an independent repairer to carry out work, as we do not automatically reimburse work arranged without our approval.

After the free labour cover ends, you may need to pay labour charges even if the faulty part remains covered. We will explain any proposed charge before you agree to a repair. You can then decide whether to proceed. We will not treat your request for advice or a warranty assessment as permission to carry out chargeable work.

If you notice a fault, contact Halvard Home and describe what has happened. Please have your purchase and delivery records available where possible. We will check whether the warranty applies and explain the next steps. Reporting a fault does not by itself confirm that a repair is covered; that decision depends on the fault and the warranty terms.

If the Lumen smart thermostat is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 67 days. The transfer deadline runs from the date of the sale. The seller should provide the original purchase and delivery records, together with a record of the sale, so the new owner can ask Halvard Home to update the warranty details.

A change of owner does not extend the warranty or change its original start date. The new owner takes over the cover attached to the Lumen smart thermostat, subject to the same terms. Please contact us if the supporting documents are unavailable, rather than assuming that the warranty has been transferred automatically.

An accepted repair does not restart the warranty. If we provide a replacement under the warranty, we will confirm how the existing cover applies to it. The warranty is separate from your statutory rights as a consumer and does not limit those rights. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the Lumen smart thermostat.

If your Lumen smart thermostat develops a fault covered by the warranty, contact Halvard Home to arrange a repair. Please describe what is happening and have your proof of purchase available. We will check the warranty cover and explain what information we need to assess the fault.

We may guide you through checks that are safe to carry out yourself. Please follow our instructions and do not open the casing, alter the wiring or attempt an internal repair. If you notice signs of overheating, damage or an electrical problem, stop using the thermostat and seek advice from us.

When we confirm that the fault is covered, we will explain how the repair will be arranged. Depending on the work needed, this may involve an engineer visiting your home or the thermostat being sent to an authorised repair centre. We will provide instructions for access, collection or packaging, as appropriate.

A warranty repair to the Lumen smart thermostat is completed within 38 working days of the fault being confirmed.

We will keep you informed about the progress of the repair using the contact details you provide. Please tell us if those details change or if there is anything that could prevent an engineer from reaching the thermostat safely. Let us know about access needs so that we can discuss suitable arrangements.

If a repair to the Lumen smart thermostat takes longer than 8 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

The loan thermostat remains the property of Halvard Home. We will explain how it will be supplied, how to use it and how to return it. Please take reasonable care of it and tell us if it develops a fault. We will also explain how to manage your account connection and personal settings when changing thermostats.

Our authorised repairers use suitable parts to restore the thermostat to proper working order. A repair may include a refurbished part that has been checked for safety and function. We will tell you what work has been carried out and whether a refurbished part has been fitted.

A refurbished part fitted to the Lumen smart thermostat is covered for 35 weeks.

If we find that the fault is not covered by the warranty, we will explain why and discuss the available options. We will ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work. You can ask us to explain the proposed work or the reason for our decision.

An engineer visit for the Lumen smart thermostat after the warranty has ended costs £105.00.

Please keep the repair record with your proof of purchase. Contact us if the thermostat still appears faulty following the repair, and describe any messages or behaviour you notice. Repair arrangements under this warranty do not affect your statutory rights.

The Keel washing machine is covered for 78 months from the date of delivery. Your cover starts when the appliance is delivered, rather than when you order it, pay for it or begin using it. Keep your delivery confirmation with your purchase receipt so that we can check when your cover began.

If your delivery record is missing or appears incorrect, contact Halvard Home. We can help you check the information held with your order. Please tell us about any difference between the recorded delivery date and the date you actually received your Keel washing machine.

The cover applies to faults that qualify for repair under the warranty. Being within the cover period does not mean that every repair is covered. We will assess the reported fault against the warranty terms and explain whether the repair is included before arranging work.

Labour for repairs to the Keel washing machine is free for the first 34 months. This applies to labour needed to carry out an approved warranty repair. It does not make work outside the warranty free, such as dealing with damage or a fault that the warranty excludes.

After the free labour cover ends, labour charges may apply even where a faulty part remains covered. We will explain any charge and ask for your agreement before chargeable work goes ahead. You can ask us to clarify what is covered before deciding whether to proceed.

Parts fitted to the Keel washing machine during a warranty repair carry their own cover. Replacement parts fitted under the warranty are covered for a further 218 days.

The replacement part’s cover starts on the date it is fitted. Keep the repair confirmation, as this records the work carried out and helps us identify the applicable cover if the replacement part develops a fault.

A warranty repair does not restart the appliance’s original cover. The replacement part’s cover runs alongside it and does not shorten any cover that still applies to the appliance. Cover for a replacement part does not extend the free labour cover.

You may pass the warranty to someone who buys your Keel washing machine. If it is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 41 days.

The transfer deadline runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the appliance’s original delivery details. A transfer does not restart or extend the cover, so the original delivery date remains relevant.

If you are unsure whether your appliance, a replacement part or repair labour is covered, contact us before booking work. We will help you check the relevant records and explain the position. This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer and does not limit them.

If your Keel washing machine develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home before arranging a repair yourself. Tell us what has happened and have your proof of purchase available. We will explain what information we need to check your cover and arrange suitable support.

We may ask you to describe warning messages, unusual sounds or changes in how the machine works. Where appropriate, we will guide you through safe checks. Do not remove panels, interfere with electrical connections or attempt work that requires an engineer. Stop using the machine if you think it may be unsafe.

An engineer will assess the fault and confirm whether the repair is covered. We will explain the assessment in plain language. If the fault falls outside the warranty, we will tell you why and discuss any proposed charges before asking you to agree to paid work.

For a covered repair, Halvard Home pays for the work and parts needed to put the fault right. We arrange the repair with an authorised engineer and keep you informed about appointments, parts availability and any change to the expected completion.

A warranty repair to the Keel washing machine is completed within 24 working days of the fault being confirmed.

Some repairs to the Keel washing machine need parts that are not held in stock. If a repair takes longer than 26 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

If a replacement is needed, we will contact you to arrange delivery and explain how to use and care for it. The replacement is supplied on loan while your repair remains outstanding. We will also arrange its collection and explain any practical requirements before delivery.

Please make sure the engineer can safely reach the machine and its connections. Remove laundry and clear belongings from the surrounding area. Tell us about access restrictions or any support you need when arranging the appointment, so we can plan the visit with you.

Refurbished parts are sometimes fitted to the Keel washing machine when new parts are scarce. A refurbished part is covered for 50 weeks.

Any refurbished part we fit must be suitable for the repair and checked for safe operation. We will explain what has been replaced and provide a record of the work. Keep this record with your proof of purchase in case you need further help.

An engineer visit for the Keel washing machine after the warranty has ended costs £61.00.

That visit charge does not mean every repair is included. We will explain any separate charges for parts or repair work and seek your agreement before proceeding. Nothing in this warranty removes your statutory rights. If you believe you are entitled to a remedy under those rights, tell us so we can consider your request on that basis.

The Ashby tumble dryer is covered for 36 months from the date of delivery. The delivery date shown on your delivery confirmation is the date we use to establish when your cover starts. Keep this document with your proof of purchase so that we can check your entitlement if you need help.

If your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation show different dates, the delivery confirmation takes priority when we calculate the cover period. If you cannot find your paperwork, contact Halvard Home. We will explain what other evidence we can accept and help you check the delivery information available to us.

Your warranty applies to faults covered by its terms. Being within the cover period does not mean that every repair, replacement or service visit is included. We will assess the reported fault against the warranty conditions and explain whether the work is covered before arranging it. Please tell us about a fault promptly, rather than continuing to use an appliance that may be unsafe.

Repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer include labour only for an opening period. Labour for repairs is free for the first 30 months. After that opening period, labour charges may apply even while the appliance remains under warranty. We will explain any proposed labour charge before you agree to a repair. Parts and labour are assessed separately, so cover for a part does not automatically mean that fitting it will be free.

Replacement parts fitted to the Ashby tumble dryer are covered for a further 245 days. This replacement part cover runs from the date the part is fitted. Keep the repair record, as it identifies the work completed and the fitting date. The replacement part cover does not shorten any protection that remains under the original appliance warranty.

Having a repair carried out does not restart the original appliance cover. The delivery date remains the reference point for that cover, while the repair record is used to establish the cover applicable to a replacement part. If you are unsure which cover applies to a reported fault, ask us to check before authorising work.

If it is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 33 days. This transfer deadline runs from the date of sale. The seller should pass the purchase, delivery and repair records to the buyer. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with those records and evidence of the sale so that we can update the warranty details.

Transferring the warranty does not restart or extend the original appliance cover. The new owner receives the cover that remains, subject to the warranty terms. We will confirm the applicable cover when the transfer has been processed.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer and does not restrict them. You may have rights against the seller even where a claim falls outside this warranty.

If your Ashby tumble dryer develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging you for the assessment, labour or replacement parts needed to put that fault right. Cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship when the appliance has been used and cared for as described in its instructions.

This policy explains how returns and refunds work at Halvard Home. It is for customers who buy directly from us for personal or household use, and for people helping them with a return. If you bought through a retailer or marketplace, please contact the seller about its returns process.

Here you can find guidance on requesting a return, providing proof of purchase, preparing goods for collection or delivery, and receiving a refund. The policy also explains how we handle goods that arrive damaged, develop a fault or do not match their description, as well as requests made because you have changed your mind.

We aim to make the process clear, fair and straightforward. Our customer support team can explain what applies to your circumstances and help if you need an accessible way to contact us. This policy does not affect your legal rights as a consumer.

You can return an unwanted appliance within 80 days of delivery. This applies if you have changed your mind, whether the appliance does not suit your home or you simply no longer want it. Please contact our customer support team to arrange the return rather than sending the appliance back without letting us know.

When you contact us, have your order confirmation ready and tell us which appliance you would like to return. We will explain how to prepare it and confirm the available return arrangements. You do not need to give a reason for changing your mind, although we welcome feedback if you would like to share it.

You may unpack and inspect the appliance as you would in a shop. Please handle it carefully and avoid using it beyond what is needed to check its nature, features and operation. If handling or use has reduced its value, we may make a deduction from your refund where the law allows. We will explain the reason for a deduction and how we have assessed it.

Please return the appliance with its supplied accessories, instructions and removable parts. Use the original packaging if you still have it. If you do not, let us know so we can advise on suitable protection. Missing packaging does not automatically prevent a return, but the appliance must be packed securely enough to protect it during transport.

Before the appliance is collected or sent back, remove your belongings and make sure it is clean, dry and safe to handle. Where relevant, disconnect it safely and remove any personal information stored on it. If disconnection requires specialist help, arrange this with a suitably qualified person. Our customer support team can explain what preparation is needed, but please do not attempt work you cannot carry out safely.

We will tell you whether collection is available and whether you will be responsible for return transport costs before you agree to the arrangements. Please tell us about access restrictions or anything that could make collection difficult. Keep your collection receipt or proof of postage until your return has been resolved.

Refunds are paid within 5 working days of a returned appliance arriving at our warehouse. We will send your refund to the payment method used for the purchase and confirm when it has been issued. Your payment provider controls when the refund appears in your account.

These terms cover returns because you have changed your mind. They do not limit your statutory rights, including rights that may apply when you cancel a purchase made online or when an appliance is faulty, damaged or not as described. If your return concerns a problem with the appliance, please tell us so we can handle it under the appropriate terms.

If your delivery arrives damaged, please contact Halvard Home so we can help. We understand that damage can be disappointing and inconvenient. We will explain the options available and arrange a suitable resolution, taking account of the condition of the delivery and your legal rights.

Report damage found on delivery within 73 hours.

Tell us what has happened and include your order reference, your contact details and a clear description of the damage. If you cannot provide photographs, tell us. We will discuss an alternative way to assess the damage rather than automatically refuse your request.

Please do not use anything that appears unsafe. Avoid attempting repairs or handling exposed or broken parts. Keep the delivery somewhere secure, away from children and pets, if you can do so safely. Tell us about any hazard so we can give appropriate advice about collection.

Keep the packaging if it is available and safe to store. It may help protect the contents during collection and support our assessment. Missing or damaged packaging will not, by itself, prevent us from helping you. Please tell us if you need suitable packaging or assistance preparing the return.

We will explain whether collection is needed and agree the arrangements with you. We cover the reasonable costs of returning a delivery that arrived damaged. Please contact us before arranging your own return service, so we can confirm a suitable method and explain how any agreed costs will be reimbursed.

Depending on the circumstances and your legal rights, you may be entitled to a repair, replacement or refund. We will discuss your preferred remedy and explain any relevant limitations. We will not require you to accept store credit instead of a refund to which you are legally entitled.

Stop using the appliance if you notice signs that it may be dangerous. Disconnect it from the power supply if this is safe to do, and keep it away from children and pets. Do not dismantle it or attempt a repair to support your return request.

This policy explains how Halvard Home manages safety concerns and recalls. It covers how we identify and assess risks, investigate reports, decide whether action is needed, and tell affected people what to do. It also sets out how we work with suppliers, retailers and relevant authorities, and how we arrange appropriate support when a recall is required.

The policy is for customers, people who use or care for our products, and anyone who may be affected by a safety concern. It also guides our staff and the organisations that design, make, supply, sell or service goods on our behalf.

Our aim is to protect people from harm through clear advice, prompt action and fair treatment. This policy explains where to raise a concern, what information may help us respond, and what to expect while we investigate and manage a safety issue.

If you believe an item supplied by Halvard Home could be unsafe, please stop using it and contact our customer support team through the contact details on our website. You can report a concern even if nobody has been hurt or you are unsure whether there is a fault.

Your safety comes before gathering evidence. If there is smoke, fire, a burning smell, exposed wiring or another sign of danger, keep away from the item. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if this is safe. If there is an immediate threat to life or property, contact the emergency services.

Do not try to recreate the problem, take the item apart or carry out a repair to help us investigate. Do not touch damaged parts or move an item if doing so could put you at risk. Keep other people and pets away from the affected area.

When reporting your concern, describe what happened, how the item was being used and whether there was an injury or damage to property. Please include your contact details and the identifying details shown on the item or its packaging, where these can be checked safely. Photographs may help, but do not put yourself at risk to take them.

You do not need proof of purchase to raise a safety concern. If you cannot find the identifying details or no longer have the packaging, please still contact us. Tell us what you know, and explain where you are uncertain. We will help you provide the information needed to assess the report.

Safety reports are answered within 27 hours. Our reply will confirm that we have received your concern and explain the next steps. An answer does not necessarily mean that the investigation is complete. We may need to ask questions or arrange an inspection before we can explain the cause.

We assess reports according to the risk described. Where appropriate, we will give instructions about safe storage, collection, inspection or disposal. Do not send an item back without speaking to us, as damage or a suspected fault may make normal handling or transport unsafe.

If our assessment identifies a wider safety issue, we may issue a safety notice or recall and work with the relevant authorities. Customers are told of a recall within 25 days of it being issued. Recall notices explain the affected items, the risk, the action customers should take and the remedy available.

We use the information in your report to investigate the concern, contact you and meet our legal duties. We may share relevant details with organisations supporting the investigation or with safety authorities, in line with our privacy policy.

Reporting a concern does not affect your statutory rights. If you are unhappy with how your report has been handled, ask customer support to refer it for review through our complaints process. Please tell us if you need an accessible way to report a concern or receive safety information.

We may recall an appliance if we identify a safety risk that needs action. A recall notice will explain the concern, how to check whether your appliance is affected and what you need to do. We will make this information available through our customer support channels and contact affected customers where we have suitable contact details.

Please read the recall notice carefully and follow its safety instructions. If your appliance is affected, stop using it unless the notice expressly says that continued use is safe. Do not attempt to repair, alter or test it yourself. Keep it away from anyone who might use it without knowing about the recall.

The notice will explain how to make the appliance safe while you arrange its return. Only disconnect or move it if you can do so safely and the instructions advise this. If you are unsure, leave it undisturbed and contact us for guidance. Do not put yourself or anyone else at risk.

You can check a recall message by contacting us through the contact details published on our website. If you think a message may be fraudulent, do not follow its links or share personal or payment details through it. We will not ask you to disclose your password to arrange a recall.

When you reply to a recall notice, please tell us how we can contact you and where the appliance is located. We may ask for identifying details from its label or a photograph so that we can confirm whether it is affected. Tell us if you cannot safely access this information.
