Use the Brio kettle only to heat drinking water in the home. Follow the instructions supplied with it and keep them available for anyone who uses it. Do not use the kettle for cooking food, heating other liquids or warming sealed containers.

Place the kettle on a dry, stable, level surface where it cannot tip or slide. Keep it away from the edge of the worktop, hot surfaces and flammable materials. Leave at least 24 centimetres of space around the Brio kettle. Make sure escaping steam cannot damage nearby cupboards or fittings.

Check that the kettle, base, plug and cable are undamaged before use. Do not use the kettle if the casing is cracked, the cable is frayed or the plug feels loose in the socket. Keep the cable clear of heat and position it so that it cannot be pulled or caught.

Use the kettle with its supplied base. Keep the electrical contacts dry and do not handle the plug with wet hands. Plug it into a suitable wall socket. Do not use an adaptor or extension lead that is damaged or unsuitable for the appliance.

Remove the kettle from its base before filling it. Follow the marked filling guides and do not operate it without water. Close the lid securely before switching it on. Do not try to defeat the lid catch, switch or automatic shut-off mechanism.

Hot water and steam can cause serious burns. Hold the kettle by its handle and keep your face and hands away from the spout. Pour carefully, without sudden movements, and do not open the lid while the water is boiling. Never carry the kettle by its cable.

Keep children away from the kettle, its cable and escaping steam. Do not allow children to play with the appliance. Anyone who needs help to use it safely should have suitable supervision. Never leave the kettle unattended while it is heating.

Switch off and unplug the kettle before cleaning or maintenance. Let the Brio kettle cool for 36 minutes before cleaning it. Do not immerse the kettle, base, plug or cable in water. Wipe the outside with a soft, damp cloth and keep moisture away from electrical parts.

Clean the air vents of the Brio kettle every 71 days. Use a soft, dry brush to remove dust from the outside of the vents. Do not push objects into them or remove protective covers. Follow the supplied instructions for descaling, and do not mix cleaning products.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, gives off smoke, smells burnt or behaves unexpectedly. Unplug it if this is safe to do. Do not attempt repairs yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice and follow any safety notice or recall instructions that apply to your Brio kettle.

Electrical safety depends on the condition of your appliance, the suitability of your home's wiring and how you use it. Follow the safety instructions supplied with your appliance. Keep those instructions accessible, and make sure anyone using the appliance understands the warnings.

Before connecting an appliance, check that the electricity supply matches the requirements shown on its rating label. Use a suitable wall socket with a secure connection. If you are unsure whether your wiring or socket is suitable, ask a qualified electrician.

Check the plug, cable and casing for visible damage before use. Do not use an appliance with exposed wires, a cracked plug, scorch marks or a loose connection. Stop using it if the cable becomes trapped, crushed or damaged.

Keep plugs, sockets and electrical connections dry. Do not handle a plug with wet hands or use an appliance where water could reach electrical parts, unless the supplied instructions expressly permit that use. Do not place cables where they could touch hot surfaces or sharp edges.

Never run an appliance from an extension lead longer than 9 metres. Connecting directly to a suitable wall socket is preferable. Do not connect extension leads together or overload sockets and adaptors. An extension lead must also be suitable for the appliance and permitted by its instructions.

Test the home's residual current device every 7 months. Follow the device manufacturer's instructions for the test procedure. If the device does not operate as expected, ask a qualified electrician to investigate. A residual current device does not make damaged equipment safe to use.

Switch off and unplug an appliance before cleaning or inspecting it, where the supplied instructions require this. Pull the plug rather than the cable. For a fixed electrical connection, follow the isolation instructions and use a qualified electrician where necessary.

Do not open electrical casings, bypass protective features or attempt repairs unless the supplied instructions specifically describe a task as suitable for the user. Electrical repairs must be carried out by a suitably qualified person using appropriate parts.

If you notice smoke, sparks, a burning smell or unusual heat around a plug or socket, stop using the appliance. Disconnect the supply only if you can do so safely. Do not touch damaged electrical parts or approach equipment standing in water.

If there is a fire, leave the area and contact the emergency services. Do not use water on an electrical fire. Do not put yourself at risk by trying to unplug burning equipment or retrieve belongings.

Report suspected electrical faults to Halvard Home through our customer support channels. Describe what happened and provide the identifying information from the appliance label, if it is safe to obtain it. Do not reconnect the appliance simply to demonstrate a fault.

If an electrical safety notice or recall applies to your appliance, follow its instructions and stop using it when directed. Do not sell, give away or dispose of an affected appliance contrary to those instructions. Contact us if you need help understanding the required action.

Choose a stable, level worktop for the Brio kettle, where it cannot be knocked or pulled over. The surface must be dry and able to withstand heat. Keep the kettle away from the edge, and make sure its handle is easy to reach without leaning across a cooking area.

The power lead of the Brio kettle is deliberately short. It must be installed within 156 centimetres of its socket. Choose a position where the plug remains accessible and the lead rests without stretching. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to make an unsuitable position work.

Keep the lead away from hot surfaces, sharp edges and places where it could be trapped or snagged. Do not leave it hanging over the worktop. Check that opening a cupboard, moving a chair or using nearby equipment will not catch the lead or disturb the kettle.

Install it at least 68 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it clear of other sources of heat and away from curtains or similar materials. Avoid placing it beneath fittings that could be damaged by escaping steam.

Do not install the kettle where splashes could reach the socket, plug or electrical connections. Keep its base dry, and do not place it in a sink or on a draining board. Use it indoors in a dry domestic setting, away from children and pets.

Before connecting the kettle, inspect the body, handle, lid, base, plug and lead for damage. Do not use it if something is cracked, loose, scorched or otherwise damaged. Contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting a repair or covering damage with tape.

Before moving the kettle, switch it off and unplug it with dry hands. Hold the plug rather than pulling the lead. Let the kettle and its contents cool, then empty it carefully. Never carry it while it is connected to the electricity supply.

Do not tilt the Brio kettle more than 56 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright and hold it securely by the handle. Carry the base separately, keeping the lead clear of your path. Do not lift the kettle by its lid or pull it along by its lead.

After moving the Brio kettle, wait 47 hours before switching it on. Leave it unplugged during this waiting period, in the position where you intend to use it. Keep the plug and base protected from water while it is standing.

Before reconnecting it, check that its new position meets the installation requirements above. Make sure the kettle sits properly on its base and that the lid closes securely. If it has been dropped, exposed to water at its electrical connections or damaged during the move, do not switch it on.

If a safety or recall notice applies to your Brio kettle, follow that notice before installing or moving it for use. Moving the appliance does not remove a safety fault. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether it is safe to reconnect.

Use the Tessa dishwasher only for washing household dishes and utensils that are suitable for dishwashing. Follow the supplied instructions and the care guidance for the items you load. Do not use it to wash items contaminated with petrol, solvents, paint or other flammable substances.

Keep the installation area dry and free from clutter. Leave at least 4 centimetres of space around the Tessa dishwasher. Do not block ventilation openings or place it where the door could obstruct a safe exit. Installation and electrical work must be carried out by a suitably qualified person in line with the supplied instructions.

Connect the Tessa dishwasher to a properly earthed socket. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor. Keep the plug and cable away from water and heat, and do not trap the cable behind the appliance. Never handle the plug with wet hands.

Check that dishes are secure and do not prevent the spray arms from moving freely. Place sharp utensils as directed in the loading instructions, with exposed points kept away from where hands could reach. Do not force the door shut or operate the appliance if the latch is damaged.

Use detergent intended for dishwashers and follow its safety instructions. Do not put washing-up liquid in the detergent dispenser. Keep detergent and rinse aid away from children and pets, and avoid contact with your skin and eyes. Do not mix cleaning products.

Keep children away from the open door and detergent dispenser. Do not allow children to play with the controls, climb inside or sit on the door. Anyone who needs support to use the appliance safely should have appropriate supervision.

Take care when opening the door during operation, as hot water and steam can cause burns. Use the pause or stop function as described in the instructions. Keep your face and hands away from escaping steam, and do not reach inside while moving parts are active.

Switch off and disconnect the appliance from the electricity supply before cleaning or carrying out user maintenance. Let the Tessa dishwasher cool for 7 minutes before cleaning it. Avoid touching surfaces that remain hot. Do not spray water onto electrical parts or immerse the plug or cable.

Clean the air vents of the Tessa dishwasher every 98 days. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and keep the filters and door seals free from trapped food and debris. Do not remove protective covers or attempt repairs yourself.

Stop using the Tessa dishwasher if it leaks, smells burnt, gives an electric shock or has damaged electrical parts. Disconnect the power only if it is safe to do so. If water is near the socket, do not touch it; seek qualified help.

Contact Halvard Home for advice about faults or safety concerns. If a recall or safety notice applies to your Tessa dishwasher, follow its instructions and do not resume use unless the notice confirms that it is safe.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you, your home and the Tessa dishwasher. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance, and keep them available for anyone who installs, disconnects or moves it. If anything is unclear, contact Halvard Home before proceeding.

Check the appliance and its packaging for signs of damage before installation. Do not connect it if the casing, door, cable, plug or hoses appear damaged. Keep packaging away from children and pets, and dispose of it through suitable local recycling or waste services.

Have the Tessa dishwasher installed by a competent installer. Electrical work and changes to plumbing must be carried out by appropriately qualified people. Do not attempt repairs or modify the appliance, its connections or its protective features to make it fit.

Choose a stable, level surface that can support the appliance during use. The location must be protected from frost, rain and direct exposure to weather. Keep ventilation openings clear, and make sure the door can open without catching on surrounding fittings.

Position the Tessa dishwasher so that its plug remains accessible after installation. It must be installed within 234 centimetres of its socket. Connect it directly to a suitable earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor, and do not trap the power cable behind the appliance.

The Tessa dishwasher must not be placed near an open flame. Install it at least 146 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep combustible materials away from the installation area, and do not use the appliance as a support for cooking equipment.

Use the inlet and drain connections specified in the installation instructions. Route hoses so that they are not kinked, stretched, crushed or caught against sharp edges. Check that connections are secure and that the water supply can be shut off without moving the appliance.

Before moving the Tessa dishwasher, switch it off, unplug it and shut off the water supply. Disconnect and drain the hoses as described in the instructions. Water may escape during disconnection, so protect the floor and keep electrical connections dry.

Remove loose contents and secure the door, racks, hoses and cable for transport. Arrange suitable help and handling equipment rather than attempting to lift the appliance unaided. Do not lift it by the door, control panel or hoses.

Do not tilt the Tessa dishwasher more than 40 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright during transport and protect it from impacts. Take care not to damage floors, doorways or the appliance when positioning it.

After moving the Tessa dishwasher, wait 36 hours before switching it on. Before use, check that it is stable, that its connections are correctly fitted and that there are no visible leaks or trapped cables.

If you notice damage, leaking water, a burning smell or unusual behaviour, stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if safe, shut off the water and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not reconnect it until the fault has been assessed and made safe.

Use the Orrin heat pump only for its intended purpose and follow the instructions supplied with it. Keep those instructions accessible and pass them on if responsibility for the appliance changes. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than guessing how to operate it.

Installation, relocation and repair must be carried out by a suitably qualified professional. Do not modify the appliance, bypass its safety controls or remove protective covers. Electrical connections and refrigerant components are not suitable for customer repairs.

Leave at least 59 centimetres of space around the Orrin heat pump. Keep the surrounding area clear of furniture, stored belongings, plants and debris. Do not cover the appliance or obstruct its air vents. Ask your installer about siting requirements that apply to your property.

Keep combustible materials and flammable substances away from the appliance. Do not use it as a shelf or drying rack. Arrange the surrounding area so that people cannot trip over connections or accidentally damage exposed pipework.

Keep children away from controls, vents and service panels. Do not allow them to climb on or play with the appliance. Anyone who needs help to use it safely should have suitable supervision and clear instructions from someone responsible for their safety.

Do not operate the Orrin heat pump if its casing, wiring or pipework appears damaged. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual noise or unexpected vibration. Isolate the electrical supply if you can do so safely, and seek professional advice.

If you suspect a refrigerant leak, keep away from the affected area and avoid flames or other ignition sources. Do not try to locate or seal the leak yourself. Contact a suitably qualified professional and follow their instructions. If there is immediate danger, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Let the Orrin heat pump cool for 33 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and isolate its electrical supply before starting. If you cannot identify the isolation point, ask your installer or Halvard Home for guidance.

Clean the air vents every 118 days. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and use suitable cleaning materials. Do not push objects through the vents, use abrasive cleaners or direct water into the appliance. Leave internal cleaning to a suitably qualified professional.

Have the Orrin heat pump safety-checked every 25 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified professional and keep the service record with your appliance documents. A scheduled check does not replace the need to report damage or changes in performance.

Do not restart an appliance that has been declared unsafe until a qualified professional confirms that it is safe to use. Follow Halvard Home safety notices and recall instructions, even if the Orrin heat pump appears to be working normally. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance.

Use the Lumen smart thermostat only for its intended purpose and in accordance with the instructions supplied by Halvard Home. Keep the instructions accessible so that anyone who operates, cleans or services the thermostat can consult them. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for guidance.

Have installation and electrical work carried out by a qualified professional. The installer should confirm that the thermostat is compatible with your heating system and suitable for the chosen location. Do not attempt to alter wiring, open the casing or bypass protective features yourself.

Leave at least 42 centimetres of space around the Lumen smart thermostat. Keep the surrounding area clear of furniture, curtains and stored belongings. Do not cover the thermostat or obstruct its air vents, as this can affect temperature sensing and allow heat to build up.

Protect the thermostat from water, condensation and direct heat. Do not place objects on it or hang items from it. If the casing becomes loose or damaged, stop using the thermostat and arrange a professional inspection rather than trying to secure it with tape or glue.

Have the Lumen smart thermostat safety-checked every 15 months. Arrange this through a qualified professional who can assess the casing, mounting, electrical connections and safe operation. Keep the inspection record with your product documents and follow advice about repairs or continued use.

Clean the air vents of the Lumen smart thermostat every 117 days. Follow the cleaning instructions supplied with the thermostat. Before cleaning, switch off the heating system and isolate the electrical supply as directed in those instructions. If you cannot do this safely, ask a qualified professional for help.

Use a soft, dry cloth to clean the outside. Do not spray cleaning products onto the thermostat, allow liquid to enter the casing or push objects into the vents. Avoid abrasive cleaners and solvents, which may damage the surface or protective casing.

Keep children from playing with the thermostat, its controls or its wiring. Anyone who needs assistance using it should have appropriate support. Explain how to recognise a fault and whom to contact, without encouraging anyone to investigate electrical parts.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or visible electrical damage, stop using the thermostat. Isolate the electrical supply if it is safe to do so. Do not touch exposed wiring. If there is a fire or an immediate danger, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Do not rely on remote access or automated settings as a substitute for checking that your home is safe. A connection problem or interrupted power supply may affect operation. Seek advice if a heating interruption could put someone at risk.

Follow safety notices and recall instructions issued by Halvard Home. If you suspect a fault, contact Halvard Home and describe what happened. Do not continue using a thermostat that has been identified as unsafe, and do not attempt an unauthorised repair.

Arrange installation and relocation of the Orrin heat pump through a qualified installer. Tell the installer about the proposed location, access to your home and concerns about the electrical supply or surrounding surfaces. Do not attempt work involving refrigerant, fixed wiring or connections that require specialist tools or training.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply safely. Ask your installer to make connected services safe for removal. Do not pull the appliance by its cable, pipework or controls. Protect exposed connections against damage and keep the route clear of obstacles.

The Orrin heat pump must be kept nearly upright when it is carried. Do not tilt it more than 24 degrees when carrying it. Use suitable lifting equipment and trained help rather than trying to support the appliance yourself. Stop the move if the appliance becomes unstable or its casing catches on a doorway or surrounding furniture.

After moving the Orrin heat pump, wait 9 hours before switching it on. This requirement also applies when the appliance has been moved within your home. If it has fallen, been laid down or suffered an impact, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than assuming it is safe to use.

The Orrin heat pump must be installed within 292 centimetres of its socket. The socket must remain accessible so the appliance can be disconnected safely. Do not stretch the power cable, trap it behind the appliance or run it where it could be crushed. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor.

Install the Orrin heat pump at least 108 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep the installation area free from combustible materials. Your installer must also check that nearby appliances, fittings and activities do not expose the heat pump to heat, grease or conditions unsuitable for safe operation.

Choose a stable location that can support the appliance and allows ventilation, servicing and safe access. Do not cover air openings or place belongings against them. Ask your installer to confirm that the position meets the installation instructions and applicable building and electrical requirements.

Do not alter the casing, remove protective covers or improvise supports to make the appliance fit. Pipework, drainage and electrical connections must be arranged as specified in the installation instructions. If the proposed position cannot meet those instructions, ask your installer to identify a suitable alternative.

Check the appliance for visible damage after delivery or relocation. If you notice a damaged cable, loose connection, unusual smell or signs of leaking, do not switch it on. Keep clear of exposed parts and contact Halvard Home or your installer for advice.

Keep packaging away from children and pets, and keep the work area clear during installation. Ask the installer to explain safe isolation and routine care before handing the appliance over. Retain the installation documents and follow safety or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home.

Safe use begins with correct installation and careful handling. Read the instructions supplied with the Keel washing machine before using it, and keep them where you can find them. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for help rather than guessing.

Leave at least 25 centimetres of space around the Keel washing machine. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, laundry and objects that could obstruct ventilation. Position the appliance on a firm, level surface, away from heat sources and places where water could reach electrical connections.

Connect the appliance only to a suitable earthed socket installed in accordance with local electrical requirements. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug accessible, and arrange the power cable so that it cannot become trapped, stretched or damaged.

Have installation and connection work carried out by a suitably qualified person if you are unsure how to proceed. Do not use the appliance if its casing, door, cable or plug is damaged, or if a hose is leaking.

Keep children and pets away from the appliance during use. Do not let children play with the controls, climb inside the drum or handle detergent. Check the drum before loading, and keep detergent and cleaning products securely stored away from children.

Use the Keel washing machine only for laundry that its instructions permit. Follow garment care labels and the guidance supplied with your detergent. Do not wash items contaminated with petrol, solvents or other flammable substances, as these can create a fire risk.

Check pockets and remove objects that could damage the drum or obstruct drainage. Make sure laundry is not caught in the door seal. Never force the door open, interfere with its lock or reach into the drum while it is moving.

Let the Keel washing machine cool for 113 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and unplug it before starting. Use the cleaning methods described in the instructions, and do not spray water onto the controls, plug or electrical connections.

Clean the air vents of the Keel washing machine every 9 days. Keep them free from lint and other debris, following the cleaning instructions. Do not push tools into openings or remove protective panels to reach internal parts.

Stop using the appliance if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual noise or unexpected movement. If safe to do so, switch it off and disconnect the power. Do not touch the plug or socket if the surrounding area is wet.

Do not attempt electrical repairs or bypass safety features. Contact Halvard Home or a suitably qualified repair professional for advice. If you receive a safety notice or recall instruction for the Keel washing machine, follow it and do not resume use unless the notice says it is safe.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you, your home and the Lumen smart thermostat. Read the supplied installation instructions before unpacking or disconnecting the device. If the instructions are missing, unclear or do not match your heating system, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting to adapt the installation yourself.

Choose a dry, stable position where the device will not be knocked, splashed or covered. Keep it away from steam, direct sunlight and sources of heat that could affect its operation. Install the Lumen smart thermostat at least 76 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Do not place it where curtains, furniture or stored belongings could obstruct access.

The Lumen smart thermostat must be installed within 263 centimetres of its socket. The socket must remain accessible so the device can be disconnected safely. Position the cable so it is not stretched, trapped, pinched or likely to cause a trip. Do not route it beneath rugs or allow it to touch hot surfaces. Use the power accessories specified in the supplied instructions.

Check that the Lumen smart thermostat is suitable for your heating system before installation. Electrical work must be carried out by a qualified electrician where required. Do not open the casing, alter wiring or bypass protective features. If you are unsure how to isolate the electrical supply safely, stop and seek professional help.

Before moving the device, switch it off and disconnect it from the socket with dry hands. Hold the plug rather than pulling the cable. Follow the supplied instructions for releasing it from its mounting. Do not force the casing or use the cable to lift or support it.

Do not tilt the Lumen smart thermostat more than 29 degrees when carrying it. Support the device securely and protect it from knocks, vibration and moisture. Use its protective packaging if available. Do not carry it with loose tools or objects that could damage the casing, controls, plug or cable.

After moving the Lumen smart thermostat, wait 45 hours before switching it on. At its new location, check that the mounting is secure, the cable is undamaged and the socket is suitable. The installation requirements also apply when returning the device to a previous location.

Do not connect or use the device if you notice cracks, loose parts, scorch marks, an unusual smell or signs of moisture inside the casing. Contact Halvard Home for guidance. Do not attempt a repair or test a damaged device by switching it on.

If Halvard Home issues a safety notice or recall affecting your Lumen smart thermostat, follow the instructions in that notice. Moving or reinstalling the device does not resolve a recall. Keep the device disconnected if the notice says to stop using it, and contact Halvard Home if you need help arranging the stated remedy.

Safe installation helps protect you, your home and your Keel washing machine. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance, and keep them available for future moves. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before starting work. Do not improvise connections or change the appliance to make it fit.

Choose a dry, sheltered position with a firm, level floor that can support the appliance during use. Keep the surrounding area clear so that the door, water supply and electrical connection remain accessible. Do not install the appliance where frost, flooding or exposure to rain could damage it.

Install it at least 93 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it away from other sources of heat, and follow the clearance guidance in the installation instructions. Do not place it where it could obstruct an escape route or prevent safe access to nearby equipment.

Check the appliance for damage before installation. If the casing, door, cable, plug or hoses appear damaged, stop and contact Halvard Home. Do not connect an appliance that has been dropped or shows signs of leaking. Keep packaging away from children and pets, and dispose of it responsibly.

Arrange for a competent installer to connect the appliance if you are unsure about the plumbing or electrical supply. The socket must be correctly earthed and suitable for the appliance. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Electrical alterations must be carried out by a qualified electrician.

Use the hoses specified in the installation instructions. Make sure they are not trapped, stretched or kinked, and secure the drain hose as directed. Remove the transport fixings before use, following the supplied instructions. Keep these fixings with the appliance documentation, as they may be needed when moving it.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off, unplug it and turn off the water supply. Disconnect and drain it as described in the instructions. Secure the door, hoses and cable so they cannot catch or trail during the move. Do not pull the appliance by its cable, hoses, door or controls.

Use trained help and suitable moving equipment to avoid injury or damage. Plan a clear route and protect the floor. Do not tilt the Keel washing machine more than 59 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright during transport and secure it against sliding or falling.

After moving the Keel washing machine, wait 44 hours before switching it on. During this wait, check that it is correctly positioned, stable and connected in line with the installation instructions. Check that transport fixings have been removed before use.

If the appliance leaks, moves unexpectedly or makes an unusual noise after installation, stop using it. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if this is safe, and turn off the water supply. Do not attempt repairs yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice before using it again.

Use the Ashby tumble dryer only as described in its instruction manual. Follow the care labels on clothing and household fabrics, and do not tumble dry items marked as unsuitable. If you are unsure whether an item is suitable, leave it out and check with its manufacturer.

Install the dryer on a stable surface in a suitable, ventilated space. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, clothing and other materials that could obstruct airflow. Do not cover the dryer or use it where doors, curtains or furnishings could block its ventilation.

Connect the dryer to a suitable wall socket, following the installation instructions. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug and socket accessible, and do not use the appliance if its cable, plug or casing is damaged. Electrical repairs must be carried out by a qualified professional.

Check pockets and remove objects before loading the drum. Do not dry items contaminated with cooking oil, solvents, fuel, wax or other flammable substances. Washing may not remove these substances completely. Follow the manual’s restrictions on materials such as foam and rubber.

Load the drum so that fabrics can move freely, following the guidance in the manual. Do not force the door shut. Choose a programme suitable for the fabric, and allow the cooling stage to finish. Do not leave warm laundry piled together where heat could build up.

Stay at home and remain awake while the dryer is operating. Keep children and pets away from the appliance, and check that the drum is clear before closing the door. Do not allow children to play with the controls or climb inside.

Let the Ashby tumble dryer cool for 111 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and unplug it before cleaning, and check that the drum and accessible surfaces are cool enough to touch safely. Follow the manual’s cleaning instructions and avoid getting electrical parts wet.

After drying, remove lint from the filter as directed in the manual. Refit the filter securely before using the appliance. Do not operate the dryer with a missing or damaged filter, and do not allow lint to collect around the appliance.

Clean the air vents of the Ashby tumble dryer every 64 days. Keep the vents unobstructed between cleans. If you notice a blockage, stop using the appliance and remove it safely in accordance with the manual.

Have the Ashby tumble dryer safety-checked every 27 months. Arrange this through a qualified service professional. Do not wait for a scheduled check if the appliance develops a fault or behaves unusually.

Stop using the dryer if you notice a burning smell, unusual noise, overheating or damage. Contact Halvard Home for advice. If there is smoke or fire, leave the door closed, get everyone outside and call the emergency services. Do not attempt repairs yourself or use an appliance covered by a stop-use recall notice.

Use the Vale fridge freezer only for storing food and drink in the home, following the instructions supplied with it. Keep those instructions accessible for anyone who uses or cares for the appliance. If you are unsure whether it is safe to use, contact Halvard Home for advice.

Place the appliance on a firm, level floor, away from heat sources and direct sunlight. Leave at least 8 centimetres of space around the Vale fridge freezer. Keep ventilation openings clear of packaging, furniture and other obstructions. Do not fit the appliance inside a cupboard unless the installation instructions expressly allow this.

Connect the appliance to an earthed wall socket that matches the electrical requirements shown on its rating label. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug accessible and make sure the power cable is not trapped, stretched or touching hot surfaces. Stop using the appliance if the cable, plug or socket appears damaged.

Have the Vale fridge freezer safety-checked every 31 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified technician. Do not attempt electrical repairs or remove protective covers yourself. A safety check does not replace attention to faults: unusual smells, smoke, sparks or repeated electrical tripping require action rather than continued use.

Clean the air vents of the Vale fridge freezer every 24 days. Switch off and unplug the appliance before cleaning, provided it is safe to reach the plug. Follow the cleaning instructions supplied with the appliance. Do not spray water into vents, controls or electrical parts, and do not use a steam cleaner.

Protect the cooling system from damage. Do not puncture internal surfaces, force tools into openings or use sharp objects to remove ice. Do not use electrical devices or apply heat inside the appliance to speed up defrosting. Follow the supplied defrosting instructions instead.

If you suspect damage to the cooling system, keep flames and ignition sources away. Ventilate the room without operating electrical switches near the appliance, and seek professional advice. Do not try to locate a leak yourself or restart the appliance until a qualified technician confirms that it is safe.

Keep children from climbing on shelves, hanging from doors or playing inside the appliance. Store packaging out of their reach. Position food and containers so that they cannot fall out when the door opens. Keep fingers clear of hinges and closing door edges.

Do not store flammable substances or explosive containers in the appliance. Follow food packaging advice about refrigeration and freezing, and keep raw food covered to prevent contamination. If cooling fails or food appears unsafe, do not taste it to check whether it is suitable to eat.

If the appliance smokes or catches fire, move away and contact the emergency services. Do not use water on an electrical fire. Follow safety notices or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home, including instructions to stop using the appliance. Contact Halvard Home if you need help understanding a notice.

Install and move the Ashby tumble dryer with care. Incorrect positioning, a damaged power lead or a blocked vent can create a risk of fire, electric shock or injury. If you are unsure whether your chosen location is suitable, ask a qualified installer before connecting the appliance.

Choose a dry, stable location where the floor can support the appliance securely. Do not install it where rain, damp or leaking pipes could reach it. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, clothing and objects that could obstruct ventilation or prevent the door from opening freely.

The Ashby tumble dryer must not be placed near an open flame. Install it at least 113 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame.

Keep the appliance away from sources of heat and combustible materials. Do not use a cupboard or enclosed space unless the installation instructions supplied with the appliance expressly permit it. Follow those instructions for ventilation, levelling and securing the appliance.

The power lead of the Ashby tumble dryer is deliberately short. It must be installed within 297 centimetres of its socket.

Connect the appliance directly to a suitable, earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to reach a socket. If the socket is unsuitable or cannot be reached without stretching the lead, ask a qualified electrician to arrange a safe connection.

Position the power lead so that it cannot become trapped, crushed or damaged behind the appliance. Keep it away from hot surfaces and sharp edges. The plug must remain accessible so that you can disconnect the appliance safely. Do not connect it if the plug, lead or socket shows signs of damage or overheating.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and unplug it by holding the plug, not pulling the lead. Follow the supplied instructions for disconnecting drainage or ventilation fittings. Secure loose fittings and keep the lead clear of the route you will use.

Arrange suitable help and lifting equipment rather than attempting to carry the appliance alone. Do not lift or pull it by its door, controls or power lead. Protect the appliance from impacts and follow the handling instructions supplied with it.

After moving the Ashby tumble dryer, wait 38 hours before switching it on.

At its new location, check that the appliance stands securely and that its ventilation openings are unobstructed. Check that connections are secure and that the lead has not been trapped during positioning. Remove transport packaging as directed in the installation instructions.

If you notice damage, a burning smell or an electrical fault, do not use the appliance. Disconnect it if safe to do so and contact Halvard Home for advice. Check the safety and recall information for the Ashby tumble dryer before putting it into use, and follow applicable instructions if it is affected by a safety notice or recall.

Use the Corra induction hob only for preparing food in a domestic setting. Read the supplied instructions before use and keep them where you can find them. If anything in the instructions is unclear, contact Halvard Home before using the appliance.

Leave at least 11 centimetres of space around the Corra induction hob. Keep this space clear of packaging, cloths, utensils and other objects. Position the appliance as directed in the installation instructions, away from water and materials that could catch fire.

Installation and electrical work must be carried out by a suitably qualified person. The electrical supply must match the requirements shown on the appliance. Do not use damaged plugs, loose sockets or extension leads. Keep the power cable away from heat and sharp edges.

Use cookware that is suitable for induction cooking and position it securely on the cooking zone. Keep pan bases and the cooking surface clean and dry. Do not heat empty cookware or allow handles to project where they could be knocked.

Stay with the appliance while cooking, particularly when heating oil or fat. Keep children away from the cooking area and prevent pets from reaching the controls or cookware. Do not rely on control locks as a substitute for supervision.

Keep metal objects, such as cutlery and lids, off the cooking surface because they may become hot. Do not use the surface for storage or as a worktop. If you have an implanted medical device, seek advice from your clinician about using induction cooking equipment.

Switch the appliance off using its controls after cooking. Do not rely on pan detection to turn it off. The surface can remain hot after cookware has been removed, so avoid touching it and keep combustible materials away.

Let the Corra induction hob cool for 114 minutes before cleaning it. Check that the surface is cold before touching it, even after this cooling period. Follow the instructions for disconnecting the electrical supply before cleaning. Never immerse the appliance or direct water into its openings.

Clean the air vents of the Corra induction hob every 16 days. Use the cleaning method described in the supplied instructions. Do not push objects into the vents or use steam cleaners, abrasive pads or cleaning products that could damage the surface.

Have the Corra induction hob safety-checked every 6 months. Arrange this through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified service provider. Do not open the casing, modify the appliance or attempt electrical repairs yourself. Keep service records with your appliance documents.

Stop using the appliance if the glass cracks, the cable is damaged, or you notice smoke, sparks or an unusual burning smell. Disconnect the electrical supply if it is safe to do so and contact Halvard Home. Do not resume use until the fault has been assessed and resolved.

If cooking oil catches fire, do not throw water on it or move the pan. Switch off the heat only if you can do so safely. If you cannot safely control the situation, leave the area, keep others away and call the emergency services.

The Vale fridge freezer must be installed and moved with care to protect you, your home and the appliance. Follow the installation guide supplied with it, including its ventilation and positioning requirements. If the guide is missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before proceeding. Do not use the appliance if it appears damaged.

Choose a dry, well-ventilated position away from direct sunlight and sources of heat. Install it at least 118 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep ventilation openings clear and follow the clearance requirements in the installation guide. Do not place the appliance where rain, splashes or damp could reach its electrical parts.

The floor must be firm, level and capable of supporting the appliance when loaded. Check that the delivery route is clear and that doorways, flooring and stairs are suitable for moving it safely. Arrange suitable help and handling equipment. Do not attempt to lift or carry the appliance without assistance, and keep children and pets away from the moving route.

Before moving the appliance, unplug it and remove food, shelves and loose fittings that could fall or cause damage. Defrost and drain it as directed in the user guide. Secure the doors without damaging the seals. Do not lift the appliance by its doors, handles, pipework or power cable. Protect the floor and avoid dragging it across the surface.

Keep the appliance upright during transport and handling. Protect the cooling pipework from knocks, crushing and punctures. If it has been tilted or laid down, leave it unplugged and ask Halvard Home for advice before reconnecting it. Do not guess when it is safe to switch it on.

Once positioned, adjust the feet as described in the installation guide so the appliance is stable and the doors close correctly. Check that the power cable is not trapped beneath the cabinet, stretched or touching hot surfaces. Fit supplied safety restraints where the guide requires them. Do not modify the cabinet, hinges or fittings to make the appliance fit.

Connect the appliance to a suitable earthed wall socket that remains accessible after installation. Do not use an extension lead or socket adaptor. If the plug, cable or socket is damaged, stop and arrange professional assessment. Electrical alterations must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Never remove the earth connection or attempt electrical repairs yourself.

If you hear escaping gas, notice oily residue around damaged cooling pipework or suspect a refrigerant leak, keep flames and ignition sources away. Avoid operating electrical switches in the affected area. Ventilate the space if it is safe to do so, leave the area and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not reconnect or use the appliance until a qualified technician confirms that it is safe.

After installation or a move, check for damage, instability and obstructed ventilation before use. Report concerns to Halvard Home rather than attempting a repair. Keep the installation guide accessible for future moves, servicing and safety checks.

The Corra induction hob must be installed by a qualified installer, with electrical work carried out by a qualified electrician. Do not connect it yourself or alter its wiring. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance and ask Halvard Home for guidance if those instructions are missing or unclear.

Before installation, check the appliance for damaged glass, loose parts, damaged cables or signs of impact. Do not install or connect an appliance that appears damaged. Keep the packaging and contact Halvard Home so that we can explain how to arrange an assessment. Do not attempt to repair damage yourself.

Choose a position where the supporting surface is stable, suitable for the appliance and able to withstand heat. Install it at least 127 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. The installer must also check the surrounding cupboards, wall finishes and fittings against the installation instructions.

Keep ventilation openings clear and make sure that stored items cannot obstruct airflow beneath the appliance. Do not fit the hob where water could reach electrical connections. Cables must be protected from heat, sharp edges and trapping. The electrical supply must be suitable, correctly earthed and fitted with appropriate protection.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off, allow it to cool and have it safely disconnected from the electrical supply. Fixed wiring must be disconnected by a qualified electrician. Remove cookware and loose accessories, and check that the route is clear of obstacles, wet flooring and anything that could cause a fall.

Arrange suitable lifting help and use handling equipment where needed. Do not lift the appliance by its cable, controls or glass edges. Do not tilt the Corra induction hob more than 54 degrees when carrying it. Protect the glass from knocks and avoid dragging the appliance across the worktop or floor.

During transport, secure the appliance so that it cannot slide, fall or strike surrounding objects. Use protective packaging that supports the appliance without pressing against vulnerable parts. Do not place items on the glass. Keep the appliance dry and protected from weather while it is being carried or stored.

After moving the Corra induction hob, wait 17 hours before switching it on. This waiting period does not replace the need for checks after transport. If the appliance has been dropped, struck or exposed to water, leave it disconnected and contact Halvard Home before arranging installation or use.

When the appliance is fitted in its new position, ask the installer to check its supports, ventilation and electrical connection. Do not use it if the glass is cracked, the controls behave unexpectedly, or you notice smoke, sparks or a burning smell. Stop using it and seek advice without touching damaged parts.

Check Halvard Home’s safety and recall information before arranging installation or moving an appliance affected by a safety notice. Follow the instructions in that notice rather than assuming relocation makes the appliance safe. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance.

Use the Fenwick cooker hood to remove cooking fumes in a household kitchen, following the instructions supplied with it. It does not replace safe cooking practices, suitable ventilation or a working smoke alarm. Keep the instructions accessible and pass them on if the appliance changes hands.

Have the appliance installed by a qualified installer. The electrical connection, fixing position and ventilation arrangements must follow the installation instructions and applicable building requirements. Do not alter the wiring, ducting or casing yourself.

Keep ventilation openings clear. If your kitchen contains a fuel-burning appliance, ask a qualified installer to confirm that extraction will not draw combustion gases back into the room. Never rely on the cooker hood to protect you from carbon monoxide.

Stay attentive when cooking, particularly when heating oil or fat. Keep flames away from the hood and do not flambé beneath it. Do not use the appliance as a shelf or hang utensils, cloths or decorations from it.

Accessible surfaces may become hot during cooking. Avoid touching the underside of the hood and keep children away from hot surfaces and moving parts. Do not allow children to play with the controls or carry out cleaning.

Switch the hood off and disconnect it from the electricity supply before cleaning or removing accessible parts. Use the isolation method described in the instructions. Do not pull on the cable, touch electrical connections with wet hands or attempt to reach an inaccessible plug.

Let the Fenwick cooker hood cool for 25 minutes before cleaning it. If surfaces still feel hot, leave them untouched until they have cooled. Use cleaning materials suitable for the surface, as described in the care instructions.

Keep water and cleaning fluid away from the motor, controls and electrical parts. Do not use steam cleaning equipment or spray cleaner into openings. Refit cleaned parts as instructed and ensure they are dry before reconnecting the electricity supply.

Have the Fenwick cooker hood safety-checked every 13 months. Arrange this through a qualified service professional. A safety check does not replace cleaning, filter care or prompt attention to faults.

Stop using the appliance if it is damaged, behaves unexpectedly, produces a burning smell or makes an unusual noise. Disconnect the electricity supply if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not remove protective covers or attempt internal repairs.

If a fire starts, do not use water on burning oil or fat and do not move the pan. Switch off the cooking heat if it is safe to do so. Leave the area and call the fire and rescue service if there is danger or you are unsure what to do.

Follow safety notices or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home. If a notice tells you to stop using the Fenwick cooker hood, leave it disconnected until the specified corrective action has been completed.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you from injury, electric shock and fire. Read the installation instructions supplied with the Fenwick cooker hood before starting work. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than guessing how to proceed.

Installation must be carried out by a suitably qualified installer. Electrical work must be handled by a qualified electrician. Do not change the plug, alter the wiring or attempt to repair electrical parts yourself. Keep the cooker hood disconnected from the electricity supply during installation.

The Fenwick cooker hood must be installed within 220 centimetres of its socket. Position it so that the plug remains accessible and the power cable is protected from heat, sharp edges and trapping. Do not stretch the cable to reach the socket or use an extension lead.

Install the Fenwick cooker hood at least 121 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. The installer must also check the hob instructions and applicable building requirements. If these requirements conflict or leave the position uncertain, seek advice before installation continues.

The supporting wall or structure must be suitable for the cooker hood. The installer must check for concealed cables and pipes before drilling and use fixings appropriate to the surface. Do not attach the cooker hood to damaged plaster, loose panels or an unsuitable support.

Ventilation and ducting must follow the installation instructions and applicable regulations. Do not connect the outlet to a flue used by an appliance that burns gas or fuel. Where extraction could affect a fuel-burning appliance, ask a qualified professional to assess ventilation and the risk of fumes entering the room.

Before moving the cooker hood, switch it off and unplug it safely. Let hot surfaces cool before handling. Arrange for a qualified professional to disconnect it if the electrical connection cannot be safely unplugged. Do not pull on the cable or ducting to release it.

Plan the route and clear away obstacles before lifting. Get help with carrying rather than attempting a lift that feels unsafe. Wear protective gloves and support the casing securely. Do not lift the cooker hood by its controls, filters, glass or power cable.

Do not tilt the Fenwick cooker hood more than 30 degrees when carrying it. Protect it against knocks and prevent it from sliding during transport. Keep the cable secured away from places where it could be crushed. Do not place objects on the cooker hood.

After moving the Fenwick cooker hood, wait 26 hours before switching it on. Before reconnecting it, have the installation checked and inspect the casing, plug and cable for damage. Do not use the cooker hood if it is loose, damaged or showing signs of overheating.

If you notice a burning smell, smoke, sparking or unusual vibration, stop using the cooker hood. Disconnect it if this is safe and contact Halvard Home. If a safety notice or recall applies to your cooker hood, follow that notice before arranging installation, moving or reuse.

Use the Mira robot vacuum only for its intended purpose: cleaning suitable indoor household floors. Follow the instructions supplied with it and check that the floor surface is suitable before cleaning. Do not use it outdoors, on wet floors or where it could come into contact with rain, splashes or standing water.

Check the Mira robot vacuum, charging dock, plug and cable for damage before use. Do not use damaged equipment or try to make it work by holding loose parts in place. Stop using it if it behaves unexpectedly, gives off an unusual smell, becomes unusually hot or makes an unfamiliar noise.

Keep the cleaning area clear of loose cables, clothing and objects that could become tangled or be dragged along the floor. Remove sharp debris and anything that could damage the vacuum or its battery. Do not use it to collect hot ash, burning material, liquids or flammable substances.

Keep children and pets away from moving parts and the charging dock. The Mira robot vacuum is not a toy. Do not allow anyone to ride on it, place objects on it or interfere with it while it is moving. Keep hair, loose clothing and fingers away from brushes and openings.

Make sure stairs, ledges and changes in floor level are protected as directed in the instructions. Do not rely on sensors where dirt, damage or the surrounding conditions could affect their operation. Keep the route to the charging dock clear and position the dock where it will not create a trip hazard.

Use only charging equipment and replacement parts approved by Halvard Home for the Mira robot vacuum. Keep the charging area dry and uncovered. Do not handle the plug with wet hands or pull the cable to disconnect it. Keep the cable away from heat and places where it could be trapped or damaged.

Switch off the Mira robot vacuum and unplug the charging dock before cleaning or maintenance. Follow the supplied instructions for removing debris and caring for the brushes, filters and sensors. Do not immerse the vacuum or dock in water, and do not apply cleaning sprays directly to electrical parts.

Clean the air vents of the Mira robot vacuum every 32 days.

Have the Mira robot vacuum safety-checked every 24 months.

Arrange safety checks and repairs through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified repairer. Do not open the battery casing, alter electrical components or bypass protective features. If the battery appears swollen, damaged or leaking, stop using the vacuum and seek advice. Avoid touching leaked material.

If you notice smoke or fire, move away and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk by attempting to move or unplug the equipment.

Check Halvard Home safety notices if you have concerns about the Mira robot vacuum. Follow recall instructions and stop using it if a notice tells you to do so. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies or need help using the vacuum safely.

Choose a dry, stable place for the Mira robot vacuum and its charging dock. Keep the area clear of clutter, loose cables and objects that could fall or obstruct its movement. Do not install it where it could block an escape route.

The Mira robot vacuum must be installed within 168 centimetres of its socket. Position the dock so that the plug remains accessible without moving furniture. The power cable must lie safely away from walkways and must not be trapped beneath the dock.

Install the Mira robot vacuum at least 101 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it away from hot surfaces, splashing water and places where steam or grease collects. Do not place the dock beside combustible materials.

Use the charging equipment supplied for the Mira robot vacuum or replacement equipment approved by Halvard Home. Check that the plug, cable and dock are undamaged before connecting them. Do not use equipment with exposed wiring, scorch marks or a cracked casing.

Plug the dock directly into a suitable wall socket. Do not run its cable beneath a rug or through a doorway where it could be crushed. If the socket is loose, damaged or unusually warm, stop using it and seek advice from a qualified electrician.

Before carrying the Mira robot vacuum, switch it off and disconnect the charging dock from the mains. Hold the plug when disconnecting it; do not pull the cable. Empty the dust container and secure removable parts as described in the user guide.

Do not tilt the Mira robot vacuum more than 51 degrees when carrying it. Support the body securely and keep it upright. Do not lift it by its bumper, cover or charging contacts, and do not carry it while it is operating.

Protect the Mira robot vacuum and its dock from knocks during transport. Use suitable protective packaging and keep the cable secured so that it cannot snag. Do not leave the appliance where it could slide, fall or be crushed.

After moving the Mira robot vacuum, wait 37 hours before switching it on. Keep it switched off and disconnected from charging during this waiting period. Leave it in a dry, stable location away from children and pets.

Before reconnecting the dock, inspect the appliance and charging equipment for damage. Make sure the charging contacts are clean and dry. If the appliance has been dropped, crushed or exposed to water, do not charge it or attempt to test it.

Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether the Mira robot vacuum is safe to install or use after moving. Do not open the casing or attempt electrical repairs yourself. If a safety notice or recall applies to your appliance, follow its instructions before installation, charging or use.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Extended Care/Safety checks under the plan
