We will agree access arrangements with you and explain what the engineer expects to do. Please tell us about access needs, communication preferences or circumstances that could affect the visit. If you rent your home, let us know whether permission from your landlord or managing agent is needed for access or work.

Our engineer will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit before starting work. If you are unsure about their identity, keep the door closed and contact Halvard Home through a trusted contact route. You do not need to admit someone whose identity you cannot confirm.

Please keep the area around the affected appliance accessible where this is safe. Keep children and pets away from the work area. The engineer may inspect the appliance, make it safe or explain why it must remain unused. We will tell you what has been found and what happens next.

Recall collections in London and South East are made within 53 working days. If a collection is needed, we will explain how it will be arranged and whether you need to prepare the appliance. Do not disconnect fixed wiring, disturb pipework or carry out removal work yourself unless we have confirmed that the task is safe and suitable for you.

If access cannot be gained or the visit cannot go ahead safely, we will explain the reason and discuss how to proceed. Tell us if your circumstances change or the reported problem becomes worse. We will review the safety advice and the arrangements with you. If you are unhappy with how your concern has been handled, our support team can explain how to raise a complaint.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Northern Ireland/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in Northern Ireland, Halvard Home can arrange a safety visit where an assessment or action at your address is needed. We will explain why the visit is required, what it involves and how to prepare. Please follow the safety advice provided with your notice.

Urgent safety visits in Northern Ireland are made within 21 hours. If you believe there is an immediate danger, move away from the affected area and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to inspect an appliance, disconnect it or recover belongings.

When you contact us about a safety concern, describe what has happened and tell us whether there is smoke, an unusual smell, visible damage or another sign of danger. We may ask for photographs, but only if you can take them safely.

If we advise you to stop using an appliance, leave it unused until we confirm that it is safe. Do not attempt repairs or ask an unauthorised person to alter it. Keep other people away where necessary, and follow the instructions in the safety notice.

We will agree access arrangements with you and explain how to recognise the person attending. Tell us about access restrictions, communication preferences or disability-related support that would help you manage the visit. You do not need to share medical details to request an adjustment.

Our representative will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit. If you are unsure about their identity, do not let them in. Contact Halvard Home through the contact details on our official website rather than relying on details supplied by an unexpected caller.

Please make the relevant area accessible if it is safe to do so. Keep children and pets away from the work area. You are not expected to move anything heavy, remove fixed fittings or carry out technical checks in preparation for our representative.

The representative will explain their findings and the action needed. This may involve making the appliance safe, carrying out an authorised repair or arranging removal. If it cannot safely be used, we will explain the restriction and provide clear instructions for you to keep.

Recall collections in Northern Ireland are made within 46 working days. We will explain the collection arrangements and tell you whether preparation is needed. Do not transport, dismantle or dispose of an appliance covered by a recall unless we have specifically advised you to do so.

If access becomes difficult or your circumstances change, please contact us so that we can review the arrangements. Tell us if the address is no longer correct or the appliance is elsewhere. We will explain how this affects the action needed to address the safety concern.

We will use the information you provide to manage the safety case, arrange attendance and keep you informed. If you are unhappy with the visit or the explanation you receive, contact our customer support team. We will review your concerns and explain how to raise a complaint.

This policy explains how Halvard Home manages servicing and engineer visits in customers’ homes. It covers requesting a visit, assessing a reported fault, arranging access, carrying out work safely and explaining the outcome. It also sets out the responsibilities of customers, engineers and service partners, including how concerns about a visit should be raised and handled.

The policy is for customers who request support from Halvard Home, people acting on their behalf, and colleagues or authorised service partners involved in arranging or delivering that support. It is intended to help everyone understand what to expect and how to prepare for an engineer’s attendance.

The policy describes our approach to respectful conduct, accessibility needs, protection of the home and personal information, and decisions about further work. It should be read alongside the terms that apply to your service arrangement and does not affect your statutory rights.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Island Areas/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in an Island Area, contact Halvard Home if you receive a safety notice or believe your appliance may be unsafe. Tell us what has happened, where the appliance is located and whether there is a risk to people nearby. We will explain the appropriate action and arrange support.

Urgent safety visits in Island Areas are made within 51 hours. When you contact us, we will assess the reported risk and confirm whether an urgent safety visit is needed. We will explain how to prepare for the visit and how to stay safe until the engineer arrives.

If there is smoke, fire or an immediate threat to life, move away from the danger and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to switch off, unplug or move an appliance. Follow the advice of the emergency services rather than attempting a repair yourself.

Where a safety notice tells you to stop using an appliance, leave it unused until we confirm that it is safe. Do not test it to see whether the fault is still present. If you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance, contact us for help checking its identification details.

Island travel can involve ferries, local transport and restricted access. Please tell us about access arrangements that could affect a visit, such as locked gates, shared entrances or landing restrictions. We will coordinate travel with the engineer and keep you informed about the arrangements for reaching your home.

We will agree how to contact you about the visit. Please let us know if you need communication support or an adjustment because of a disability or health condition. You do not need to explain private medical details unless they are relevant to arranging safe access or providing suitable support.

The engineer will identify themselves and explain the safety work before starting. You can ask us to verify their identity before letting them into your home. Please keep the route to the appliance clear where it is safe to do so, and keep children and pets away from the work area.

Recall collections in Island Areas are made within 44 working days. If collection is required, we will explain how it will be arranged and whether the appliance needs to be disconnected. Do not disconnect fixed wiring or fittings yourself unless our instructions expressly say that this is safe.

You do not need to take an unsafe appliance to a ferry terminal, depot or collection point unless we have agreed a safe arrangement with you. Tell us if moving it would create a risk or if you cannot prepare it for collection.

After a visit or collection, we will explain what happens next and provide confirmation of the action taken. If you remain concerned about safety or are unhappy with the arrangements, contact Halvard Home and ask for your case to be reviewed.

You can request an engineer visit by contacting Halvard Home through the contact options on our website. Tell us what needs attention, describe the fault and explain whether it affects safe use. We may ask questions to help us understand the problem and arrange suitable support.

Please provide your name, contact details and the address where the engineer is needed. Let us know about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything else that could affect the visit. If you need support with communication or access, tell us when booking so we can discuss suitable arrangements with you.

We may suggest checks that could resolve the issue without a visit. Only carry out checks that you understand and can perform safely. Do not remove protective covers, attempt repairs or continue using anything that appears unsafe. Tell us if you cannot follow the suggested checks.

Standard engineer visits are booked within 16 working days of a request. We will discuss availability with you and confirm the agreed booking using the contact details you provide. Your request is not a confirmed booking until you receive our confirmation. Please check the details and contact us if they are incorrect.

Each visit is given an arrival window of 5 hours. The arrival window will be included in your booking confirmation. We cannot guarantee arrival at a particular point within that window. If travel disruption or an earlier job affects the engineer’s arrival, we will contact you to explain and discuss the booking.

A responsible adult who can authorise access and discuss the fault must be present for the visit. Please make sure the engineer can reach the area safely and has space to work. Keep pets away from the work area and tell us about hazards that may require special arrangements.

We will explain whether the visit is covered by your guarantee or service agreement. If charges may apply, we will explain the basis of those charges before you agree to the booking. The engineer will seek your approval before carrying out chargeable work outside what has already been agreed.

Please contact us if you need to change or cancel your booking. Tell us if your contact details or access arrangements change. If the engineer cannot gain access or cannot work safely, the visit may need to be rearranged. We will explain any applicable charges before you agree to the booking.

Booking a visit does not guarantee that the fault will be resolved during attendance. The engineer may need to assess the issue, obtain parts or arrange specialist support. We will explain the outcome of the assessment and discuss what happens next, including whether a further booking is needed.

We use the information you provide to arrange and manage your visit in line with our privacy notice. Nothing in these booking terms limits your statutory rights. If you are unsure about the booking arrangements, please contact us so we can explain them before you agree to proceed.

We will explain the charges that apply to your booking before you agree to an engineer visit. These may include a call-out charge, labour, parts and any specialist work needed. Prices quoted to you include VAT where it applies, unless we clearly state otherwise.

A call-out charge covers the engineer’s attendance and assessment of the reported fault. It may still be payable if you decide not to proceed with a repair. We will tell you whether this charge applies when you book, including where a repair may be covered by your warranty.

Labour after the first hour is charged at £55.00 an hour. The engineer will explain how labour charges are calculated and ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work. You can ask for clarification before deciding whether to proceed.

An estimate reflects the information available when we assess the work. If the engineer finds that the repair needs different parts or further work, we will explain the revised charges and seek your approval. We will not carry out that work without your agreement.

Parts fitted outside the warranty carry a handling charge of 28%. We calculate this charge from the price of the parts and show it separately on your bill. We will explain the parts charges before asking you to approve the repair.

Where a fault is covered by your warranty, we will apply the warranty terms to the visit and repair. If we believe a charge is payable because the fault is not covered, we will explain why and give you the opportunity to discuss our assessment.

A charge may apply if the engineer cannot safely access the property or the place where the work is needed. We will explain any access requirements when arranging your visit. Please tell us about anything that could prevent the engineer from carrying out the agreed work.

If you need to cancel or rearrange your booking, please contact us. Any cancellation charge must have been explained when you booked and will reflect reasonable costs incurred. We will explain the reason for the charge rather than applying it without an explanation.

Payment is due as agreed when you book or approve the work. We will confirm the available payment methods and provide a bill describing the charges. Please do not make payments to an engineer unless we have confirmed that they are authorised to collect payment.

If you believe your bill is incorrect, contact us using the details on your booking confirmation. Tell us which charge you are questioning and why. We will review the bill, explain our findings and correct any error. These charging terms do not affect your statutory rights.

Cancel a visit at least 56 hours before it is due to avoid a charge. A visit cancelled later than that is charged at £47.00.

If you need to cancel, please contact Halvard Home using the contact details in your booking confirmation. Tell us that you want to cancel and provide enough information for us to find your booking, such as your name and the address where the engineer was due to attend.

We use the date and time we receive your cancellation request to decide whether the cancellation charge applies. You do not need to wait for us to reply for your request to count as received, provided it reaches the contact channel shown in your booking confirmation.

Please make your request clear. Asking a question about your booking does not cancel it. If you are unsure whether you still need the visit, we can help you understand your options, but the booking remains in place unless you ask us to cancel it.

We will confirm your cancellation using the contact details held with your booking. Please keep that confirmation for your records. If you do not receive it, contact us so that we can check the booking status. We will not charge you simply because our confirmation was delayed.

If you would prefer to rearrange the visit, please tell us rather than cancelling without explanation. We will explain the available options and whether moving the booking would attract the cancellation charge before making the change. A replacement appointment is subject to engineer availability.

If someone else is contacting us on your behalf, we may need to check that they have your permission to cancel. This helps us protect your booking and personal information. Please make sure they have the details needed for us to identify the visit.

Where a cancellation charge applies, we will explain why and tell you how payment will be handled. If you have already paid towards the visit, we will explain how the cancellation affects that payment and whether a refund is due.

We understand that unexpected circumstances can make it difficult to keep an appointment. If this happens, please contact us and explain your situation. We will consider the circumstances fairly, including any accessibility needs, and let you know whether we can waive the cancellation charge.

You will not be charged for a cancellation made by Halvard Home. If we cannot carry out the visit as agreed, we will contact you to explain what has happened and discuss rearranging it or cancelling the booking.

If you believe a cancellation charge has been applied incorrectly, please contact us with your booking details and any relevant correspondence. We will review the information and explain our decision. Nothing in these cancellation terms limits your statutory rights.

The Brio kettle should be serviced every 44 months. This schedule helps keep your kettle in good working order and gives an engineer an opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults that may not be obvious during everyday use.

Use the purchase date to work out when your kettle is due for its initial service. After a service has been completed, use the service date as the starting point for the next scheduled visit. Keep your purchase receipt and service records somewhere accessible.

If you do not know the purchase date or cannot find your service record, contact Halvard Home. We can help you check the information available and agree an appropriate service date. Do not assume that a previous owner arranged servicing if you bought your kettle used.

A reminder is sent 4 weeks before the Brio kettle is due for a service. Please keep your contact details up to date so that the reminder can reach you. You remain responsible for arranging a service if you do not receive it.

To arrange a visit, contact Halvard Home through our customer support service. Tell us that you would like to book a routine service for your Brio kettle. Please also mention any changes in its performance or any damage you have noticed.

A routine service of the Brio kettle takes about 135 minutes. Please allow the engineer access to the kettle throughout the appointment. Tell us when booking if access to your home is restricted or if you need adjustments to help you manage the visit.

A routine service of the Brio kettle costs £78.00. This covers the scheduled inspection and routine servicing work. If the engineer identifies a repair outside that work, we will explain what is needed and ask for your agreement before proceeding.

Before the engineer arrives, unplug the kettle, allow it to cool and empty it. Leave it with its base in a clear, accessible area. Have your service record available if you have it, and keep children and pets away from the work area.

The engineer will check the kettle’s condition and operation, carry out routine servicing and explain any findings. If the kettle needs further attention, the engineer will tell you whether it is safe to use and what action is recommended.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the kettle leaks, gives off a burning smell or has visible damage to its cable, plug or casing. Stop using it and contact Halvard Home for advice. Unplug it only if you can do so safely.

Routine servicing does not replace the cleaning and care described in the user instructions. Follow that guidance between visits, and keep the engineer’s service notes with your records so they are available when you arrange future servicing.

Common repairs to the Brio kettle include problems with heating, the switch, the lid and the filter. A kettle that leaks, cuts out unexpectedly or fails to switch off may also need attention. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether the fault can be resolved through routine care or needs an engineer’s assessment.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, smells of burning, has a damaged lead or shows signs of electrical damage. Disconnect it from the mains if it is safe to do so. Do not open the casing, alter the plug or attempt an electrical repair yourself. Keep the kettle disconnected until we advise that it is safe to use.

If the kettle is noisy, heats poorly or pours unevenly, limescale or a blocked filter may be responsible. Follow the cleaning and descaling instructions supplied with your kettle. Let it cool before cleaning, and keep the base, plug and electrical connections dry. Do not use sharp tools to remove deposits or force a stiff lid or switch.

Replace the filter of the Brio kettle every 18 weeks. Use a compatible replacement supplied or approved by Halvard Home, and follow the fitting instructions. If the filter does not sit securely, stop using the kettle and contact us. Damage to the filter housing may need assessment rather than a replacement filter.

When requesting a repair, describe the fault and tell us about visible damage, unusual smells or leaking. We may ask for proof of purchase and details from the product label. This helps us check the support available and decide whether an engineer visit is suitable. Do not reconnect an unsafe kettle to demonstrate a fault.

We will explain the proposed repair and any applicable charges before asking for your agreement. The engineer will inspect the kettle and confirm whether the work can proceed safely. If the inspection reveals a different fault or changes the proposed work, we will explain the revised recommendation and seek your approval before proceeding.

Paid repairs to the Brio kettle come with their own guarantee. Repairs are guaranteed for 122 days. This guarantee covers the work carried out and the parts fitted as part of that repair. Contact us if the repaired fault returns, and keep your repair confirmation. The repair guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Spare parts for the Brio kettle are stocked for 9 years after the model is discontinued. Availability of a suitable part will be checked when we assess your request. We will tell you if a required part is unavailable and explain the options rather than fit an unsuitable substitute.

If the kettle cannot be repaired safely, we will explain why and discuss the appropriate next steps. The engineer may advise against further use. Follow that advice and keep the kettle disconnected. We can also provide guidance on responsible disposal of electrical appliances.

Routine servicing helps keep your Tessa dishwasher working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to check its condition. Follow the servicing guidance supplied with your appliance and arrange a visit when your service reminder arrives. If you cannot find your guidance, contact Halvard Home for help with your servicing schedule.

Owners of the Tessa dishwasher are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 6 weeks before a service is due.

Keep your contact details up to date so that your reminder reaches you. Tell Halvard Home if your email address, postal address or preferred contact method changes. If you believe a service is due but have not received a reminder, contact us rather than waiting for a message.

A reminder does not confirm an appointment. You need to contact Halvard Home through the booking details provided to arrange an engineer visit. We will confirm the appointment and explain the arrangements for access. Tell us about accessibility requirements or anything that could affect the engineer’s ability to reach the appliance safely.

A routine service of the Tessa dishwasher takes about 230 minutes.

Please allow the engineer to complete the agreed checks without interruption. An adult who can provide access and discuss the appliance must be present for the visit. If you need to change or cancel the appointment, contact Halvard Home using the details in your booking confirmation.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the dishwasher and make sure the area around it is clear. Keep children and pets away from the working area. Leave the appliance installed unless Halvard Home has specifically asked you to do otherwise. Do not disconnect pipework, remove panels or attempt to move a fitted appliance yourself.

During the service, the engineer will inspect the appliance and carry out the maintenance covered by your booking. Tell the engineer about changes in washing performance, unusual noises, leaks or messages shown on the controls. This helps them understand concerns that may not be apparent during an inspection.

Routine servicing is different from a repair visit. If the engineer finds a fault that falls outside the agreed service, they will explain the findings and discuss the proposed work with you. Work that carries a separate charge will require your agreement before it proceeds.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the dishwasher appears unsafe. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell or water leaking near electrical connections. Contact Halvard Home for advice, and avoid touching plugs or switches if the surrounding area is wet.

After the visit, keep the service record with your appliance documents and follow the engineer’s advice. Continue the cleaning and care described in the user guide between services. A service does not replace routine care, and routine care does not replace the checks carried out by an engineer.

Common repairs to the Tessa dishwasher include clearing blockages, replacing worn seals, repairing door catches and replacing faulty pumps, valves or heating components. An engineer will assess the fault before recommending a repair. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm which parts are needed from a description alone.

When you contact Halvard Home, describe what happens when you use the appliance, including any unusual noise, leak, smell or message on the display. Tell us whether the problem affects washing, draining, heating or closing the door. This helps us prepare for the visit, but does not replace an inspection.

You can check that the water supply is turned on, that the door closes properly and that accessible filters are clear, following the user instructions. Do not remove panels, disconnect internal wiring or attempt to repair electrical components. If the appliance leaks, smells of burning or appears electrically unsafe, stop using it and isolate it from the electricity supply if safe to do so.

Diagnosing a fault on the Tessa dishwasher costs £77.00 if no repair follows. This applies where the engineer identifies the fault but you choose not to proceed, or where a repair is not practical. We will explain any applicable charge before you agree to the visit.

If a repair is possible, the engineer will explain the proposed work and provide a quote before starting it. The quote will identify the labour and parts covered. You can decline the repair. We will not carry out additional chargeable work without your agreement.

Some faults can be resolved by cleaning, adjustment or securing a loose connection. Others need replacement parts. If the engineer finds damage or an installation problem that prevents safe repair, they will explain what needs attention. Work to your household plumbing, electrical supply or cabinetry is not included unless expressly agreed.

Spare parts for the Tessa dishwasher are stocked for 19 years after the model is discontinued. A part may still need to be ordered for your repair. We will explain any availability issue and discuss the available options before arranging further work.

Repairs to the Tessa dishwasher are guaranteed for 184 days. The guarantee covers the repair work and parts supplied as part of that work. It does not cover an unrelated fault or damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or unauthorised alterations. Your statutory rights are not affected.

If the repaired fault returns, contact Halvard Home and describe the symptoms. Have your repair confirmation available so we can review the work recorded and advise on the appropriate next step. Do not arrange chargeable work elsewhere on the assumption that we will reimburse it.

Please make the appliance accessible and clear the surrounding floor before the engineer arrives. Empty the dishwasher and keep pets away from the work area. After the repair, the engineer will check its operation, explain any care advice and leave a record of the work completed.

The Orrin heat pump should be serviced every 42 months. Servicing helps keep it working safely and efficiently and gives a qualified engineer an opportunity to identify wear, check its condition and explain whether repairs are needed.

You are responsible for arranging servicing and keeping a record of the work carried out. Contact Halvard Home if you need help finding a suitable engineer or checking when your service is due. Have your service record available so that we can give advice based on its history.

If you do not know when the Orrin heat pump was last serviced, contact us for guidance. Do not assume that an installation visit, repair or inspection included a service. The paperwork should clearly describe the work completed and state whether servicing formed part of the visit.

Servicing must be carried out by an engineer with the appropriate training and qualifications for the work involved. Tell the person arranging your appointment that the visit is for an Orrin heat pump. Explain whether you have noticed unusual noises, warning messages, changes in performance or visible damage.

A service is intended to assess the condition and operation of the Orrin heat pump. The engineer will carry out the checks and maintenance appropriate to its installation and the servicing instructions. They should explain their findings in plain language and make clear whether further investigation or repair is recommended.

Routine servicing does not replace the need to report a fault. If you think the Orrin heat pump is unsafe, stop using it if you can do so safely and contact us for advice. Do not remove protective covers, interfere with electrical connections or attempt work that requires a qualified engineer.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the Orrin heat pump safely. Keep the surrounding area clear and tell us about access restrictions when arranging the visit. Let us know if you need support with communication or access so that suitable arrangements can be discussed.

Tell the engineer about repairs, alterations or changes to the installation that could affect the service. Share relevant paperwork where available. This helps the engineer understand the condition of the Orrin heat pump without relying on assumptions about work carried out by someone else.

The engineer should discuss work outside the agreed service with you and explain the approval process. Any applicable charges should be explained before you agree to additional work. A service appointment does not automatically authorise repairs or replacement parts.

Keep the service report with your installation and repair records. Check that it describes the work completed, the findings and any recommended action. If something is unclear, ask for an explanation. An accurate service history helps you plan servicing and gives engineers useful information when assessing a concern.

If your Orrin heat pump is not heating properly, is making an unusual noise or is showing a fault message, contact Halvard Home to arrange support. Tell us what you have noticed and whether anything has changed in how the appliance operates. This helps us prepare for the visit and identify suitable parts.

Before booking an engineer, we may ask you to check the controls, confirm that the power supply is available and look for anything blocking airflow. Only carry out checks that are safe and described in your user guide. Do not remove covers or attempt work on electrical components, pipework or refrigerant connections.

Diagnosing a fault on the Orrin heat pump costs £88.00 if no repair follows. We will explain the applicable charges when arranging your visit. After inspecting the appliance, the engineer will describe the fault and explain the proposed repair, including the parts required and the price, before asking for your approval.

Common repairs can include replacing faulty sensors, repairing control connections and addressing problems with fans or circulation components. The work needed depends on the engineer’s findings. Symptoms that appear similar can have different causes, so we cannot confirm the repair or the parts required from a description alone.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the Orrin heat pump safely. Clear nearby belongings and keep children and pets away from the work area. Let us know about restricted access, parking arrangements or other circumstances that could affect the visit. If access is unsafe, the engineer may need to stop work.

Where suitable parts are available and conditions allow, the engineer will carry out the agreed repair during the visit. If parts need to be ordered, we will explain what happens next and arrange a return visit with you. We will seek your approval before carrying out work beyond the repair you have accepted.

Repairs to the Orrin heat pump are guaranteed for 211 days. This guarantee covers defects in the repair work and replacement parts supplied as part of that repair. Contact us if the repaired fault returns, and keep your repair confirmation available so we can review the work carried out.

The repair guarantee does not cover unrelated faults, accidental damage, misuse or damage caused by unauthorised alterations. We will explain our findings if a reported problem falls outside the guarantee. Your statutory rights are not affected by this repair guarantee.

Replace the filter of the Orrin heat pump every 23 weeks. Follow the user guide when choosing and fitting a replacement filter. If you cannot access the filter safely or are unsure which replacement is suitable, contact us for advice rather than forcing any fittings.

After the repair, the engineer will check operation where it is safe to do so and explain any care instructions. If the Orrin heat pump cannot be used safely, leave it switched off until we confirm that it is safe to use.

The Lumen smart thermostat should be serviced every 29 months. This schedule helps keep the thermostat working reliably and gives an engineer the opportunity to check its condition, controls and connection to your heating system. Servicing does not replace any separate maintenance required for the heating system itself.

The service schedule normally runs from the installation date or the date of the most recent completed service. Keep your installation paperwork and service records so that you can check when your thermostat is due for attention. If those records are missing, contact Halvard Home for help with confirming your service schedule.

A reminder is sent 12 weeks before the Lumen smart thermostat is due for a service. We use the contact details held on your customer account, so please tell us if these change. Check that messages from Halvard Home can reach you, including by reviewing your email filtering settings where appropriate.

The reminder is a prompt to arrange a visit, rather than confirmation that an appointment has been booked. You remain responsible for arranging servicing if a reminder does not reach you. Contact us if you believe your thermostat is due for a service but have not received a reminder.

A routine service of the Lumen smart thermostat costs £182.00. This covers the routine checks described when you book. If the engineer identifies a fault that needs work outside the routine service, we will explain the proposed work and any associated charge before asking for your agreement.

To arrange servicing, contact Halvard Home through the support details provided with your thermostat or on our website. Tell us about any warning messages, unusual behaviour or changes to your heating controls. This helps us understand whether a routine service is suitable or whether you need a fault assessment instead.

Please make sure the engineer can safely reach the thermostat and any related controls needed for the checks. Clear belongings from the working area and keep pets away while the visit is under way. Tell us when booking if access is restricted or if you have accessibility requirements.

An adult authorised to agree to the work must be available for the visit. The engineer will explain any access needed and discuss anything that could prevent the service from being completed. We will advise you about rearranging the appointment if the work cannot proceed safely.

After the service, the engineer will explain the findings and any recommended action. Keep the service record with your thermostat paperwork and check that your customer details remain correct.

Do not wait for scheduled servicing if the thermostat appears damaged or is behaving unexpectedly. Contact Halvard Home for advice and avoid opening the casing or attempting internal repairs yourself. If you have concerns about the safety of your heating system, stop using the affected equipment where safe to do so and seek professional assistance.

Common repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat include correcting an unresponsive display, restoring its connection to your home network and resolving faults that prevent it from controlling your heating. An engineer will check the reported problem and explain whether it can be repaired. Some symptoms may come from your heating system or network rather than the thermostat itself.

Before arranging a visit, check that the thermostat has power and that your home network is working. Follow the troubleshooting guidance supplied with the thermostat, but do not remove its casing or attempt to alter electrical connections. If you notice scorching, an unusual smell or exposed wiring, stop using the thermostat and contact us for advice.

When you contact us, describe what you can see on the display and how your heating is behaving. Tell us about any changes to your network, heating controls or electrical supply that may be relevant. We may suggest checks that you can carry out safely, or arrange an engineer visit where an inspection is needed.

Diagnosing a fault on the Lumen smart thermostat costs £75.00 if no repair follows. Before repair work starts, the engineer will explain the fault, the proposed work and the charge that applies. You can decide whether to proceed. If you decline the repair, the engineer will explain any precautions needed to leave the thermostat safe.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the thermostat and any relevant heating controls safely. Clear away belongings that could obstruct access, and keep pets away from the work area. If access depends on permission from a landlord or building manager, arrange that permission before the visit. Tell us about access needs when booking.

The Lumen smart thermostat has a filter that wears out with use. Replace the filter every 10 weeks. Use a suitable replacement and follow the instructions supplied with the thermostat. Do not wash or reuse a worn filter unless those instructions expressly allow it. If the filter housing is damaged or difficult to open, ask us for advice rather than forcing it.

Repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat are guaranteed for 140 days. If you believe a repair has failed, contact us and describe the symptoms. We will assess whether the issue relates to the work carried out. Keep your repair confirmation so that we can identify the work and explain how the guarantee applies. Your statutory rights are unaffected.

Spare parts for the Lumen smart thermostat are stocked for 10 years after the model is discontinued. The engineer will check which parts are needed and confirm availability before agreeing the repair arrangements. If a suitable part cannot be supplied, or a repair would not leave the thermostat safe and reliable, we will explain the available options without carrying out unapproved work.

Common repairs to the Keel washing machine include clearing drainage blockages, replacing worn door seals and repairing faults with the door lock, water inlet or drum mechanism. The engineer will check the appliance and explain what is causing the problem before recommending work.

Diagnosing a fault on the Keel washing machine costs £38.00 if no repair follows. If a repair is possible, the engineer will explain the proposed work and provide a quote. We will ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable repairs.

Your quote will explain the charges for labour and any parts needed. If the engineer discovers a different fault during the repair, they will discuss any change to the work or price with you before proceeding. You may decline the proposed repair.

If your machine is not draining, check the drain hose for visible kinks and follow the user guide for checking the filter. Switch the appliance off and unplug it before carrying out any checks. Do not force the filter open if the water inside may be hot.

Replace the filter every 25 weeks. Use a compatible replacement and follow the fitting instructions in the user guide. If the filter is stuck, damaged or difficult to reach safely, leave it in place and contact us for advice.

Leaks may come from the door seal, a hose connection or an internal component. Stop using the machine if you notice water escaping. Turn off the water supply if you can reach the tap safely. Do not touch the plug or socket if the surrounding area is wet.

Unusual scraping, grinding or movement can indicate a trapped object or a fault with the drum assembly. Stop the programme if it is safe to do so. Do not remove cabinet panels or attempt to repair internal electrical or moving parts yourself.

When arranging a visit, describe the symptoms and tell us about any warning message shown on the display. Let us know if the machine is built into cabinetry or access is restricted. This helps us plan the work and identify parts that may be needed.

Please clear the route to the appliance and keep pets away from the working area. The engineer will need safe access to the machine and its connections. If access is unsafe, they will explain what needs to change before work can proceed.

Spare parts for the Keel washing machine are stocked for 18 years after the model is discontinued. The engineer will confirm which part is suitable and whether it is available for your repair. If a part needs ordering, we will explain how the repair will be arranged.

After completing the repair, the engineer will check the machine’s operation and explain any care advice relevant to the fault. Keep the repair record with your appliance documents. If the problem remains or returns, contact us and describe what is happening.

The Keel washing machine should be serviced every 32 months. Use the installation date as the starting point for your servicing schedule. After a routine service, use the date recorded by the engineer to plan when your next service is due.

Keep your installation paperwork and service records somewhere accessible. These records help you follow the schedule and give the engineer useful information about previous work. If you do not know when your Keel washing machine was installed or last serviced, contact Halvard Home for guidance.

Arrange your service through Halvard Home so that we can confirm the work required and allocate a suitable engineer. When booking, tell us about any changes in performance, unusual sounds, leaks or messages shown on the display. Please also mention any repairs or alterations already carried out.

A routine service of the Keel washing machine takes about 122 minutes. This is a guide to the service work, rather than a guaranteed appointment length. Access difficulties or faults found during the visit may affect how the appointment proceeds. The engineer will explain any changes before continuing.

A routine service of the Keel washing machine costs £168.00. We will confirm what the routine service includes when you book. Repairs, replacement parts or work outside that scope may involve an additional charge. We will explain any proposed charge and ask for your agreement before carrying out that work.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the drum and make sure the area around the Keel washing machine is clear. Leave the controls, door and connections accessible. Do not move the appliance or disconnect its water or electricity supply unless Halvard Home has asked you to do so.

Tell us when booking if access involves stairs, restricted space or building entry arrangements. Let us know about any adjustments you need to make the visit accessible. Keep children and pets away from the working area while the engineer is carrying out the service.

During the service, the engineer will inspect the appliance, check its operation and look for signs of wear or leakage. They will explain any concerns and advise whether further work is needed. A routine service does not automatically include the repair of faults.

Do not wait until your scheduled service if you notice a problem. Stop using the Keel washing machine if you suspect it is unsafe, and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not remove covers or attempt internal repairs yourself.

After the visit, keep the service record and follow any care or safety advice the engineer provides. Servicing supports the ongoing care of your Keel washing machine but does not replace the cleaning and maintenance described in its user guide. Contact Halvard Home if anything in the service record is unclear.

The servicing schedule for your Ashby tumble dryer is intended to help keep it safe and working properly. Follow the service due date shown in your service record. If you cannot find your record or are unsure whether a service is due, contact Halvard Home for advice.

Your recommended schedule takes account of how the appliance is used and the conditions in which it operates. Tell us if your use has changed or if the dryer has been moved to a different location. An engineer can advise whether the schedule needs to be reviewed.

Owners of the Ashby tumble dryer are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 3 weeks before a service is due.

Please keep your contact details up to date so that we can send your reminder to the correct address. A reminder does not confirm an appointment. You need to contact us to arrange a visit and agree suitable access to your home.

A routine service of the Ashby tumble dryer takes about 62 minutes. This is a guide rather than a guarantee, as access difficulties or the condition of the appliance may affect the work. Tell us about any known faults when booking so that we can plan the visit appropriately.

A routine service of the Ashby tumble dryer costs £98.00. This covers the routine servicing work agreed when you book. If the engineer identifies a fault requiring work outside that scope, we will explain the proposed repair and any additional charge before asking for your approval.

Routine servicing includes inspecting accessible components, checking operation and looking for signs of wear or damage. The engineer will explain any findings that need your attention. Servicing does not replace the cleaning and care described in the user instructions, including keeping filters and accessible ventilation areas clear.

Before the visit, make sure the engineer can reach the dryer safely. Remove laundry from the drum and clear nearby belongings. Let us know about restricted access, parking arrangements or any support you need when arranging the appointment. Do not move or disconnect the appliance if doing so would be unsafe.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or damage to the electrical connection. Stop using the dryer and disconnect it from the electricity supply if safe to do so. Contact Halvard Home for advice about inspection or repair.

After the service, the engineer will record the work completed and explain any recommendations. Keep the service record with your appliance documents and check the recorded service due date. If you need to change a booking or have missed a service, contact us to agree a suitable appointment.

If your Ashby tumble dryer is not heating, is making an unusual noise or has a drum that will not turn, contact Halvard Home to arrange a service visit. Describe what happens when you try to use it, including any warning shown on the display. This helps us prepare for the visit.

Stop using the appliance if you notice smoke, a burning smell, damage to the power cable or signs of overheating. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if it is safe to do so. Do not remove the casing or attempt to repair electrical components yourself.

Before booking, check that the door closes properly and that the filter and accessible airflow openings are clear, following the user guide. A blocked filter or trapped item can affect drying performance. Do not keep restarting the appliance if the fault remains or you are concerned about its safety.

Diagnosing a fault on the Ashby tumble dryer costs £41.00 if no repair follows. The engineer will explain the fault and tell you whether a repair is possible. You will receive a repair quote for approval before chargeable repair work begins. You can decline the repair without agreeing to further work.

Common repairs include replacing worn drive belts, faulty heating components, damaged door catches and failed sensors. The work needed depends on the engineer’s findings. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm the repair or its cost from a description alone.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Clear the surrounding floor and remove laundry from the drum. Tell us when booking if the appliance is difficult to access or has been installed in a confined space. Do not move it yourself if doing so could cause injury.

Replace the filter of the Ashby tumble dryer every 8 weeks. Use a compatible replacement supplied or approved by Halvard Home, and follow the fitting instructions. Replacement does not remove the need to clean the filter as directed in the user guide. Ask us for advice if the filter does not fit securely.

Spare parts for the Ashby tumble dryer are stocked for 13 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for your repair will be checked when the fault has been identified. If a required part cannot be supplied, we will explain what this means and discuss the available options with you.

Paid repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer come with their own guarantee. Repairs are guaranteed for 105 days. Contact us if you believe the repair has failed, and keep your repair confirmation available. We will assess whether the reported problem relates to the work covered by that guarantee.

The engineer will explain what has been repaired and any care instructions that apply. If the appliance is unsafe to use, they will tell you and explain the next steps. Nothing in this policy affects your statutory rights.

The Vale fridge freezer should be serviced every 8 months. This schedule helps us check that your appliance is working safely and as intended. Please arrange servicing even if you have not noticed a problem, as some faults may not be obvious during normal use.

Your service schedule is based on the installation date recorded with Halvard Home and is updated when a scheduled service is completed. If you do not know when your service is due, contact us so we can check your record and help you arrange a suitable appointment.

A reminder is sent 9 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held on your customer record, so please tell us if these change. You remain responsible for arranging the appointment if a reminder does not reach you.

A routine service of the Vale fridge freezer takes about 154 minutes. This is a guide rather than a guaranteed completion time. The engineer may need to investigate further if they find a fault, have difficulty accessing the appliance or identify a safety concern.

A routine service of the Vale fridge freezer costs £177.00. We will explain what is included when you book. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are not included unless we expressly confirm otherwise. We will seek your agreement to any additional charges before that work begins.

During the service, the engineer checks the appliance’s condition and operation, including accessible seals, controls and drainage. They may also inspect ventilation and look for signs of wear or damage. The checks depend on safe access and the condition of the appliance.

Please keep the area around the Vale fridge freezer clear and make sure the engineer can reach it safely. Tell us about restricted access, parking difficulties or anything else that could affect the visit. We will let you know if any preparation is needed before the appointment.

Do not move the appliance, disconnect it or remove food unless we ask you to do so. If the engineer needs access to a compartment, they will explain what is required. Please make suitable arrangements to protect food if the appliance needs to be switched off.

If you notice unusual noises, poor cooling, leaks or damage, contact us rather than waiting for your scheduled service. A routine appointment is not a substitute for reporting a fault. If you believe the appliance is unsafe, stop using it and seek advice.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact us so we can discuss availability and explain any applicable cancellation terms. After the visit, we will provide a service record, explain any findings and confirm how these affect your servicing arrangements. Keep this record with your appliance documents.

Common repairs to the Vale fridge freezer include replacing damaged door seals, clearing drainage blockages and repairing cooling controls. An engineer will assess the fault and explain the proposed work. Some symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm the repair needed from a description alone.

If the appliance is not cooling properly, check that the power supply is working and that food or packaging is not blocking the internal vents. Make sure the doors close securely. Do not remove covers, interfere with wiring or attempt to repair the cooling system yourself.

Water inside the cabinet, unusual ice build-up or a door that will not stay closed may need an engineer’s attention. Changes in sound can also indicate a fault, although some operating noises are normal. Tell us what you have noticed and whether the appliance displays a warning.

When arranging a visit, describe the problem and provide the appliance details from its rating label. Let us know about access restrictions or anything that could make moving the appliance difficult. Please keep the route to the appliance clear and secure pets away from the work area.

Diagnosing a fault on the Vale fridge freezer costs £31.00 if no repair follows. The engineer will explain their findings and provide a repair quotation where a repair is possible. We will ask for your agreement to the proposed charges before carrying out chargeable repair work.

The quotation will describe the work and parts required. If further faults become apparent, the engineer will explain any change to the proposed repair and seek your approval. You can decline additional work. We will explain any applicable diagnostic charge before you decide whether to proceed.

Repairs are guaranteed for 297 days. This guarantee covers faults in the repair work and replacement parts supplied for that repair. It does not cover unrelated faults, accidental damage or problems caused by misuse. Contact Halvard Home if you believe a completed repair has failed. Your statutory rights are not affected.

Replace the filter of the Vale fridge freezer every 19 weeks. Use a compatible filter and follow the fitting instructions supplied with it. Incorrect fitting can cause leaks or affect performance. If you cannot remove or fit the filter safely, ask us for advice rather than forcing it.

Spare parts for the Vale fridge freezer are stocked for 14 years after the model is discontinued. The engineer will confirm which part is needed and whether it is available for your repair. If the repair cannot be completed, we will explain the reason and discuss the options with you.

Keep food safely stored while the appliance is not working properly, and follow food safety advice if you are unsure whether it remains safe to eat. If you notice smoke, a burning smell or damaged electrical wiring, stop using the appliance and disconnect it from the power supply if safe to do so.

The Corra induction hob should be serviced every 16 months. Use the installation date as the starting point for your servicing schedule. After a service, use the date recorded by the engineer to plan your next appointment. Keep the service record with your appliance documents so that you can check when servicing is due.

Arrange servicing through Halvard Home or an engineer qualified to work on induction hobs. When booking, explain that the appointment is for routine servicing of the Corra induction hob. Tell the booking team about any changes in performance, unusual sounds, visible damage or messages shown on the controls. This helps the engineer prepare for the visit.

A routine service of the Corra induction hob takes about 120 minutes. The engineer will need clear access to the hob and the area beneath it. Tell the booking team if access is restricted by fitted furniture, stored items or other features of your kitchen. The expected scope of the visit should be confirmed when you book.

A routine service of the Corra induction hob costs £210.00. This covers the routine checks and servicing work agreed at booking. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are not included unless expressly agreed. If the engineer identifies work that would involve an additional charge, they will explain what is needed and seek your approval before proceeding.

Before the engineer arrives, stop using the hob and allow it to cool. Remove cookware and loose items from the surface, and clear the surrounding worktop. Make sure the engineer can reach the electrical isolation switch safely. Do not remove panels, loosen fittings or attempt to disconnect the appliance yourself.

Routine servicing includes an inspection of the hob’s condition, controls and accessible electrical connections. The engineer will check for signs of damage, overheating or wear and assess whether the hob operates as expected. The checks carried out may depend on the installation and the condition of the appliance.

Servicing does not replace normal cleaning and care. Follow the care instructions supplied with the Corra induction hob and use suitable cookware. Keep ventilation openings clear and avoid using the surface for storage. If you are unsure whether a cleaning method or material is suitable, ask Halvard Home for advice.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if you notice cracked glass, smoke, a burning smell or an electrical fault. Stop using the hob, isolate it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home for guidance. Do not use it again until a qualified engineer has confirmed that it is safe.

After the visit, the engineer will provide a record of the work completed and explain any findings or recommended action. Keep this record for future reference. If servicing could not be completed, contact the booking team to agree what needs to happen before another appointment can be arranged.

Common repairs to the Corra induction hob include replacing damaged controls, repairing heating faults and resolving problems with the cooling fan. An engineer will assess the fault before recommending a repair. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm which part is needed from a description alone.

If the hob does not respond, check that its power supply is switched on and that the controls are clean and dry. Check the user guide for advice about the control lock and suitable cookware. Do not remove covers, interfere with wiring or attempt to repair internal components yourself.

Stop using the hob if the glass is cracked, there is a burning smell or the appliance repeatedly trips the electrical supply. Switch it off at the isolator if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Do not continue cooking while waiting for advice.

When booking a visit, describe what happens when you try to use the hob. Tell us about any visible damage, unusual sounds or messages on the display. We may ask for proof of purchase and information from the appliance label so that we can check cover and prepare for the visit.

Diagnosing a fault on the Corra induction hob costs £80.00 if no repair follows. We will explain any applicable charges when arranging the appointment. After assessing the appliance, the engineer will explain the proposed work and provide a quote where the repair is chargeable. Work will not proceed without your agreement.

Please make sure the engineer can safely reach the hob, its electrical isolator and the cupboard space beneath it. Remove cookware and personal belongings from the work area. Tell us when booking if access is restricted or if the appliance has been altered, as this may affect the work we can undertake.

Repairs may involve replacing the glass surface, a control component, a heating component or a fan. The engineer will use suitable replacement parts and check that the repaired appliance operates safely. If repair is not appropriate, we will explain the reason and discuss the available options without committing you to further work.

Repairs are guaranteed for 150 days. The repair guarantee covers faults arising from the work carried out or the replacement parts supplied. It does not cover unrelated faults, accidental damage or misuse. Contact us if the repaired fault returns. This guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Keep the hob clean using the methods described in the user guide. If your installation includes an extraction filter, follow the care instructions for that filter. Replace the filter every 24 weeks. Cleaning and routine filter replacement are maintenance tasks rather than repairs, unless an underlying fault requires an engineer’s attention.

Spare parts for the Corra induction hob are stocked for 5 years after the model is discontinued. We will confirm whether the part needed for your repair is available when arranging the work. If a part must be ordered, we will explain how this affects the visit and keep you informed about your booking.

The Fenwick cooker hood should be serviced every 38 months. This schedule helps keep the appliance operating safely and supports reliable extraction. Servicing is intended to assess its condition, identify wear and confirm whether maintenance or repairs are needed. It does not replace the cleaning and care described in your user guide.

Your service due date is based on the installation record or the date of the previous completed service, as appropriate. Keep your installation documents and service records somewhere accessible. If you do not know when servicing is due, contact Halvard Home so we can check the information held for your appliance.

A reminder is sent 5 weeks before the Fenwick cooker hood is due for a service. We use the contact details held on your customer record, so please tell us if these change. The reminder is a prompt to arrange servicing, not confirmation that an engineer visit has been booked.

You remain responsible for arranging the service if a reminder does not reach you. Please contact Halvard Home if you believe your appliance is due for servicing but have not heard from us. We can help clarify its service status and explain how to request an appointment.

When arranging your visit, tell us about changes in performance, unusual sounds, visible damage or concerns about the controls. Explain any access restrictions that could affect the engineer’s work. This helps us prepare for the visit and assess whether the reported problem needs attention separately from the planned service.

Servicing must be carried out by an engineer with suitable competence for the appliance and the work involved. The engineer will assess the accessible components, check operation and explain relevant findings. Work outside the agreed service scope requires your approval. We will explain applicable charges before you agree to proceed.

Please make the area around the Fenwick cooker hood accessible and remove objects that could obstruct safe working. Follow the booking instructions about preparing the appliance for inspection. Do not dismantle the hood, remove electrical covers or attempt repairs yourself. Leave technical checks and adjustments to a suitably qualified engineer.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the appliance appears unsafe. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell, exposed wiring or signs of electrical damage. Isolate it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home for guidance.

After servicing, keep the engineer’s report with your appliance records and follow the advice provided. If repairs are recommended, ask whether the Fenwick cooker hood can be used safely while arrangements are made. Contact Halvard Home if the report is unclear or if you need help confirming the updated service due date.

Common repairs to the Fenwick cooker hood include faults with extraction, lighting, controls and the fan. Halvard Home can arrange an engineer visit to investigate these problems and explain the recommended repair. When you contact us, describe the fault and tell us whether you have noticed unusual noise, smells or visible damage.

Poor extraction may be caused by a blocked filter or an obstruction in the ventilation route. Check the accessible areas described in your user guide, without removing fixed covers or reaching into ducting. Replace the filter every 14 weeks. Follow the guide when choosing and fitting a replacement filter.

Before cleaning the hood or handling an accessible filter, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply. If you cannot disconnect it safely, leave the work to an engineer. Do not open electrical housings, alter wiring or try to repair the motor yourself.

If the light fails, check your user guide to find out whether the light fitting is intended for customer replacement. Do not force a cover or fit an unsuitable replacement. Where the fitting is sealed, damaged or not described as replaceable by the customer, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment.

Rattling, scraping or vibration can indicate a loose fitting, an obstruction or a fan fault. Stop using the hood if the noise is unusual or persistent. Do not continue running it to test whether the problem clears. An engineer can inspect the mounting, fan and accessible internal components.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, sparks or damage to the power cable, stop using the hood and disconnect the supply if it is safe to do so. Do not touch exposed wiring or attempt a repair. Contact Halvard Home for advice before using the hood again.

When arranging a visit, we will ask about access to the hood and the nature of the fault. Please tell us about restricted access, fragile surfaces or installation features that could affect the work. Clear the cooking area and leave the hob switched off and cool for the visit.

The engineer will inspect the hood and discuss the proposed work with you. We will explain applicable charges and seek your agreement before carrying out chargeable repairs. If the fault involves the property’s wiring or ventilation rather than the hood, we may advise you to contact a suitably qualified tradesperson.

Spare parts for the Fenwick cooker hood are stocked for 8 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for your repair will be checked when the fault and required component have been identified. If a suitable part cannot be supplied, we will explain the position and discuss the available options.

After a repair, the engineer will check the affected functions and explain whether the hood is safe to use. Keep the repair record with your purchase documents. If the fault returns or you remain concerned about the hood’s operation, contact Halvard Home and describe what has happened.

Regular servicing helps keep your Mira robot vacuum working reliably and gives an engineer the opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults. Follow the servicing advice supplied with your appliance and any recommendations made after an engineer visit. Your service due date will be shown in your service record.

A reminder is sent 7 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held on your customer account, so please keep these up to date. If your details change or you do not receive a reminder, contact Halvard Home to check your service due date.

A reminder does not confirm an appointment. Please contact us to arrange a suitable visit when your service is due. We will confirm the appointment details and explain any preparation needed. Tell us about access restrictions or anything that could affect the engineer’s ability to work safely in your home.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum takes about 164 minutes. This is a guide rather than a guaranteed completion time. The condition of the appliance, access to its parts and any problems found during inspection may affect how the visit proceeds. The engineer will explain if further work is needed.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum costs £115.00. We will confirm what is included when you book. Repairs, replacement parts or work outside the routine service will be discussed with you separately. We will explain any proposed charges and ask for your agreement before carrying out additional work.

Before the visit, make sure the Mira robot vacuum and its charging dock are accessible. Clear the surrounding floor space and keep pets away from the work area. Please have any relevant service records available and tell the engineer about unusual noises, charging problems, warning messages or changes in cleaning performance.

During the service, the engineer will inspect the appliance, check its operation and assess components that may need attention. Cleaning and adjustments covered by the routine service will be carried out where appropriate. The engineer will also explain any care tasks you should continue between service visits.

Servicing does not replace the cleaning and maintenance described in the user instructions. Keep the appliance in suitable condition and use it as directed. If you notice damage, overheating, a burning smell or another safety concern, stop using it and contact us rather than waiting for a scheduled service.

After the visit, we will provide a record of the work completed and any recommendations. Keep this with your appliance documents. If another visit is needed, we will explain why and discuss the arrangements with you. Contact us if you need to change a booking or have questions about your servicing schedule.

Common repairs to the Mira robot vacuum include clearing blocked airways, replacing worn brushes, repairing wheels and resolving charging faults. Problems with movement or cleaning can also be caused by dirt on sensors, tangled hair or a filter that needs attention. Before arranging a repair, we may ask you to carry out safe checks to help identify the fault.

Switch the appliance off and disconnect the charging dock from the mains before cleaning accessible parts. Empty the dust container, remove loose debris and check that brushes and wheels can move freely. Follow the care instructions supplied with your appliance. Do not open sealed covers, interfere with electrical connections or try to repair a damaged battery.

Replace the filter of the Mira robot vacuum every 13 weeks. A clogged or damaged filter can reduce cleaning performance and put strain on the appliance. Use a compatible replacement and fit it as described in the care instructions. If you are unsure whether a filter is suitable, ask Halvard Home before using it.

If the Mira robot vacuum will not charge, check that the dock is connected securely and that its contacts are clean and dry. Stop using the appliance if you notice a burning smell, unusual heat, swelling or damage to a cable. Disconnect it from the mains if it is safe to do so and contact us for advice.

When you contact Halvard Home, describe the fault and tell us about any damage or changes in performance. We may ask for proof of purchase and photographs of the affected area. Please do not send an appliance or remove internal parts unless we have explained how to proceed. We will advise whether an engineer visit or another repair arrangement is appropriate.

Before work begins, we will explain the proposed repair and whether you will need to pay. If an engineer discovers a different fault, we will discuss any change to the work and seek your agreement before carrying out chargeable repairs. You can decline the proposed work, and we will explain what that means for returning or safely using the appliance.

For an engineer visit, make the Mira robot vacuum and its charging dock accessible. Keep the working area clear and secure pets away from it. Tell us about access restrictions when arranging the visit so that we can discuss suitable arrangements.

Repairs to the Mira robot vacuum are guaranteed for 223 days. If a repaired fault returns, contact Halvard Home and provide the repair record if available. We will assess the problem and explain how the repair guarantee applies. This guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Halvard Home keeps spare parts for the Mira robot vacuum after it stops being sold. Spare parts are stocked for 6 years after the model is discontinued. Availability can depend on the part required. If a suitable part cannot be supplied, we will explain the options available rather than fit an unsuitable substitute.

Routine servicing helps keep your appliance working as intended and gives you an opportunity to discuss concerns with a qualified engineer. Under Extended Care, you can arrange servicing through Halvard Home, subject to your membership being active and the appliance being eligible under your plan.

Extended Care members get 63% off routine services. The discount applies to the routine service charge for an eligible appliance. We will explain what the service includes and confirm the price before you agree to a booking. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are covered only where your plan terms expressly include them.

To request a service, contact our customer support team through the contact details shown in your membership documents. Please have your membership details available and tell us about the appliance, its location and any concerns you would like the engineer to investigate.

Extended Care members are offered a visit within 2 working days. This is an offer of an appointment, rather than a guarantee that servicing or repair work will be completed at that visit. We will discuss the available appointment with you and confirm the booking when you accept it.

Please tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or adjustments that would help you use our service. If someone is arranging the visit on your behalf, we may need your permission before discussing your membership or confirming work with them.

Before the engineer arrives, make sure the appliance is accessible and the surrounding area is safe to work in. Keep pets away from the work area. Please do not move heavy equipment, disconnect fixed connections or attempt work that could put you at risk.

The engineer will explain the checks included in the service and ask about how the appliance has been working. They may need to operate it, inspect accessible components and carry out routine maintenance appropriate to its condition. Servicing does not guarantee that faults will not develop.

If the engineer identifies a fault or recommends work outside the agreed service, they will explain the findings and discuss the proposed action. Where a charge would apply, we will explain it and seek your agreement before proceeding. You can decline chargeable work without losing your routine servicing discount.

If the engineer finds a safety concern, they will explain what you should do and may advise you to stop using the appliance. Please follow that advice and do not restart or reconnect it unless it is safe to do so.

We will provide a record of the service, including relevant findings and recommendations. Keep this with your membership documents. If you need to change or cancel a booking, contact us so we can explain your options and any applicable booking conditions.

If you are unhappy with the service or believe something has been missed, contact customer support. We will review your concerns and explain the next steps. Your rights under consumer law are not affected by your membership or by using this servicing benefit.

result.text:
Extended Care Plus members get 14% off routine services. The discount applies to the routine service charge when your membership is active and the appliance being serviced is covered by your plan. Please tell us that you are a member when you book so that we can check your cover and apply the discount.

Routine servicing helps keep your appliance in good working order. It includes checks, cleaning and adjustments that are appropriate for the appliance and can be carried out safely during the visit. A service does not replace repairs where a fault is found.

Extended Care Plus members are offered a visit within 4 working days. This means we will offer an appointment within that window, rather than guarantee that servicing or repairs will be completed within it. If the appointment does not suit you, we will help you arrange a suitable alternative.

When booking, please describe any concerns about how your appliance is working. Tell us about warning messages, unusual smells, leaks or damage, as these may affect whether a routine service is appropriate. We may recommend a repair visit instead and will explain how this affects your booking.

We will confirm what the service includes and explain any charges before you agree to the booking. Work outside the routine service is not automatically included in your plan. We will explain the proposed work and ask for your agreement before carrying it out.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Clear the surrounding area and tell us about anything that could make access difficult, such as restricted parking, stairs or a fitted enclosure. Do not move a heavy appliance yourself if doing so could cause injury or damage.

An adult who can authorise the agreed work must be present for the visit. Please keep children and pets away from the work area and let the engineer know about any relevant safety concerns. Tell us when booking if you need adjustments to help you communicate with us or manage the visit.

The engineer may be unable to proceed if access is unsafe, the appliance cannot be isolated safely, or its condition makes servicing unsuitable. If this happens, we will explain the reason and discuss what needs to change before another visit can be arranged.

If the engineer finds a fault, they will explain what they have found and whether the appliance can be used safely. Repairs may require a separate booking or replacement parts. We will check your cover and explain any applicable charges before asking you to approve the work.

Please contact us if you need to change or cancel your appointment. We will explain any cancellation terms that apply to your booking. If we need to change the visit, we will let you know and help arrange an alternative.

After the service, we will provide a record of the work carried out and any recommendations. Keep this with your plan documents, and contact us if anything in the service record is unclear.
